  subroutine wrlist(listz, nlistz)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: listz(*)
    integer, intent(in) :: nlistz
    character(len=82) :: line
    integer :: index, il, numstart, numend

    ! initialise the output line and bookkeeping index
    line = ' '
    index = 1
    numstart = listz(1)

    do il = 2, nlistz
       if (listz(il) = listz(il-1) + 1) then
          numend = listz(il-1)
          call add_range_to_line(numstart, numend, line, index)
          numstart = listz(il)
       end if
    end do

    ! handle the final range
    numend = listz(nlistz)
    call add_range_to_line(numstart, numend, line, index)

    ! print the remaining contents of the line
    if (index > 1) then
       write(*,'(A)') line(1:index-1)
    end if

  end subroutine wrlist

  subroutine add_range_to_line(numstart, numend, line, index)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in)    :: numstart, numend
    character(len=*), intent(inout) :: line
    integer, intent(inout) :: index
    integer :: ncharrange, ncharend
    character(len=24) :: rangestring
    character(len=12) :: endstring

    ! convert the starting number to characters
    call int_iwrite(rangestring, numstart, ncharrange)

    ! if this is a true range, append "-<end>"
    if (numend > numstart) then
       call int_iwrite(endstring, numend, ncharend)
       rangestring(ncharrange+1:ncharrange+1) = '-'
       rangestring(ncharrange+2:ncharrange+1+ncharend) = endstring(1:ncharend)
       ncharrange = ncharrange + 1 + ncharend
    end if

    ! If the new range would exceed 80 characters, flush the current line
    if (index + ncharrange > 80) then
       write(*,'(A)') line(1:index-1)
       line = ' '
       index = 1
    end if

    ! prepend a comma unless this is the first range on the line
    if (index > 1) then
       line(index:index) = ','
       index = index + 1
    end if

    ! copy the range string into the output line
    line(index:index+ncharrange-1) = rangestring(1:ncharrange)
    index = index + ncharrange

  end subroutine add_range_to_line

  subroutine int_iwrite(str, num, nch)
    implicit none
    character(len=*), intent(out) :: str
    integer, intent(in)          :: num
    integer, intent(out)         :: nch
    character(len=24) :: temp

    write(temp,'(I0)') num
    nch = len_trim(temp)
    str(1:nch) = temp(1:nch)

  end subroutine int_iwrite

end program wrlist_demo

    0.0_dp, 0.5_dp, 0.0_dp, &
    0.0_dp, 0.0_dp, 0.5_dp /

  ! composite with matrix tensor cm, inclusion tensor ci and Eshelby

  !===================================================================
  subroutine tenadps(a, cm, ci, s)
    real(dp), intent(out) :: a(:,:)
    real(dp), intent(in)  :: cm(:,:), ci(:,:), s(:,:)
    real(dp) :: temp1(3,3), temp2(3,3), temp3(3,3)
    integer :: i, j

    ! temp1 = ci - cm
    do i = 1, 3
       do j = 1, 3
          temp1(i,j) = ci(i,j) - cm(i,j)
       end do
    end do

    ! temp2 = inv(cm)
    call matxinv(temp2, cm, 3)

    ! temp3 = temp2 * temp1
    call matxmul(temp3, temp2, temp1, 3)

    ! temp1 = s * temp3
    call matxmul(temp1, s, temp3, 3)

    ! temp1 = I + temp1 (add 1 on diagonal)
    do i = 1, 3
       temp1(i,i) = 1.0_dp + temp1(i,i)
    end do

    ! a = inv(temp1)
    call matxinv(a, temp1, 3)

  ! Simple 3×3 matrix multiplication: C = A * B
  !===================================================================
  subroutine matxmul(c, a, b, n)
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    real(dp), intent(out) :: c(n,n)
    real(dp), intent(in)  :: a(n,n), b(n,n)
    integer :: i, j, k
    real(dp) :: sum

    do i = 1, n
       do j = 1, n
          sum = 0.0_dp
          do k = 1, n
             sum = sum + a(i,k) * b(k,j)
          end do
          c(i,j) = sum
       end do
    end do

  !===================================================================
  ! Subroutine: matxinv
  ! Inverts a 3×3 matrix using the Gauss‑Jordan method with partial
  ! pivoting.  The input matrix 'a' is not modified; the inverse is
  ! returned in 'ainv'.
  !===================================================================
  subroutine matxinv(ainv, a, n)
    integer, intent(in) :: n

    real(dp) :: piv, factor, tmp

    aug(:,1:n) = a
    aug(:,n+1:2*n) = 0.0_dp
    do i = 1, n
       aug(i,n+i) = 1.0_dp
    end do

    ! Gauss‑Jordan elimination with partial pivoting
    do k = 1, n
       ! Find pivot row
       ipiv = k
       maxrow = k
       piv = abs(aug(k,k))
       do i = k+1, n
          if (abs(aug(i,k)) > piv) then
             piv = abs(aug(i,k))
             ipiv = i
          end if
       end do
       if (piv == 0.0_dp) then
          print *, 'WARNING: Singular matrix encountered in matxinv.'
          ainv = 0.0_dp
          return
       end if
       ! Swap rows if needed
       if (ipiv /= k) then
          aug([k,ipiv],:) = aug([ipiv,k],:)
       end if
       ! Normalize pivot row
       factor = aug(k,k)
       aug(k,:) = aug(k,:) / factor
       ! Eliminate other rows
       do i = 1, n
          if (i /= k) then
             factor = aug(i,k)
             aug(i,:) = aug(i,:) - factor * aug(k,:)
          end if
       end do
    end do

    ! Extract inverse
    ainv = aug(:,n+1:2*n)

  end subroutine matxinv

    REAL, PARAMETER :: LC = 2.501E6        ! latent heat of condensation (J/m3)
    REAL, PARAMETER :: LF = 0.334E6        ! latent heat of fusion (J/kg)
    REAL, PARAMETER :: HCAPW = 4180.0      ! specific heat of water (J/kg/K)
    REAL, PARAMETER :: HCAPI = 2100.0      ! specific heat of ice (J/kg/K)
    REAL, PARAMETER :: RHO_ICE = 917.0     ! density of ice (kg/m3)
    REAL, PARAMETER :: DPSIDT = 114.3      ! d(ice potential)/dT (m/K)
    REAL, PARAMETER :: ZERODEGC = 273.15   ! K
    REAL, PARAMETER :: SNOW_HCAP = 0.63E6  ! J/K/m3 (snow heat capacity)

    IF (LTIMER) CALL TIMER('HEATCAP ',3)

    ! Initialise output array – soil points get their own HCAP, ice points
    ! receive the constant snow heat capacity.
    DO I = 1, NPNTS
       IF (V_SAT(I) > 0.0) THEN
          HCAPS(I) = HCAP(I)
       ELSE
          HCAPS(I) = SNOW_HCAP
       END IF
    END DO

    ! -----------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Compute auxiliary temperature and moisture diagnostics for soil points
    ! -----------------------------------------------------------------
    DO J = 1, SOIL_PTS
       I = SOIL_INDEX(J)
       TSL(I)     = TSOIL(I) - ZERODEGC
       SMCLSAT(I) = RHO_WATER * DZ * V_SAT(I)
       SMCLF(I)   = SMCLSAT(I) * STHF(I)
       SMCLU(I)   = SMCL(I) - SMCLF(I)
    END DO

    ! -----------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Main loop: compute TMAX, DTHU and the effective heat capacity
    ! -----------------------------------------------------------------
    DO J = 1, SOIL_PTS
       I = SOIL_INDEX(J)

       ! TMAX – temperature above which all water is unfrozen
       IF (SMCL(I) > SMCLSAT(I) * EPSILON(SMCL(I))) THEN
          TMAX(I) = -SATHH(I) / DPSIDT * (SMCLSAT(I) / SMCL(I))**B(I)
       ELSE
          TMAX(I) = -ZERODEGC
       END IF

       ! Rate of change of unfrozen moisture with temperature
       IF (TSL(I) >= TMAX(I)) THEN
          DTHU(I) = 0.0
       ELSE
          DTHU(I) = DPSIDT * SMCLSAT(I) / (B(I) * SATHH(I) * RHO_WATER * DZ) &
               * (-DPSIDT * TSL(I) / SATHH(I))**(-1.0/B(I) - 1.0)
       END IF

       ! Effective heat capacity (J/m3/K)
       HCAPS(I) = HCAP(I) + (HCAPW - HCAPI) * SMCLU(I) / DZ &
            + HCAPI * SMCL(I) / DZ &
            + RHO_WATER * DTHU(I) * ((HCAPW - HCAPI) * TSL(I) + LF)
    END DO

    IF (LTIMER) CALL TIMER('HEATCAP ',4)

         LIT_C_L(L) = G_LEAF(L)*LEAF(L) + G_ROOT(N)*ROOT(L) + G_WOOD(N)*WOOD(L)

         PC(L) = NPP(L) - LIT_C_L(L)

         DLIT_DLAI = (G_LEAF(L)*LEAF(L) + G_ROOT(N)*ROOT(L)) / LAI(L) &
                & + B_WL(N)*G_WOOD(N)*WOOD(L) / LAI(L)

         FPAR = (1.0_dp - exp(-KPAR(N)*LAI(L))) / KPAR(N)
         DFPAR_DLAI = exp(-KPAR(N)*LAI(L))

         DNPP_DLAI(L) = NPP(L)*DFPAR_DLAI/FPAR &
                & + (1.0_dp - R_GROW(N))*RESP_W(L) &
                & * (DFPAR_DLAI/FPAR - B_WL(N)/LAI(L))

         LAMBDA_G = 1.0_dp - (LAI(L) - LAI_MIN(N)) / (LAI_MAX(N) - LAI_MIN(N))
         DLAMG_DLAI = -1.0_dp / (LAI_MAX(N) - LAI_MIN(N))

         PC_G(L) = LAMBDA_G * NPP(L) - LIT_C_L(L)
         DPCG_DLAI(L) = LAMBDA_G*DNPP_DLAI(L) + DLAMG_DLAI*NPP(L) - DLIT_DLAI
         DPC_DLAI(L)   = DNPP_DLAI(L) - DLIT_DLAI
      end do

      ! Store current total veg carbon for later differencing
      do T = 1, LAND_PTS
         L = LAND_INDEX(T)
         DCVEG(L) = LEAF(L) + ROOT(L) + WOOD(L)
      end do

      call GROWTH(LAND_PTS, LAND_INDEX, N, DPCG_DLAI, FORW, GAMMA, &
           & DENOM_MIN, PC_G, LEAF, ROOT, WOOD)

      ! Update change in vegetation carbon
      do T = 1, LAND_PTS
         L = LAND_INDEX(T)
         DCVEG(L) = LEAF(L) + ROOT(L) + WOOD(L) - DCVEG(L)
      end do

      ! Final diagnostics and implicit corrections
      do T = 1, LAND_PTS
         L = LAND_INDEX(T)
         DLAI = LEAF(L)/SIGL(N) - LAI(L)
         PC_S(L) = PC(L) + FORW*DPC_DLAI(L)*DLAI - DCVEG(L)*GAMMA

         FPAR = (1.0_dp - exp(-KPAR(N)*LAI(L))) / KPAR(N)

      end do

        & GAMMA, DENOM_MIN, PC_G, LEAF, ROOT, WOOD)
      implicit none
      integer, intent(in) :: LAND_PTS, LAND_INDEX(POINTS), N
      real(dp), intent(in) :: DPCG_DLAI(POINTS), FORW, GAMMA, DENOM_MIN
      real(dp), intent(in) :: PC_G(POINTS)
      real(dp), intent(inout) :: LEAF(POINTS), ROOT(POINTS), WOOD(POINTS)

      integer :: I, L
      real(dp) :: DENOM, DLEAF, DROOT, DWOOD
      real(dp) :: DL_DW, DLAI_DW, DR_DW, NUMER
      real(dp) :: WOOD_MAX, WOOD_MIN

      do I = 1, LAND_PTS
         L = LAND_INDEX(I)

         ! Increment to wood carbon
         DL_DW = LEAF(L) / (B_WL(N)*WOOD(L))
         DR_DW = DL_DW
         DLAI_DW = DL_DW / SIGL(N)

         NUMER = PC_G(L)
         DENOM = (1.0_dp + DL_DW + DR_DW)*GAMMA - FORW*DLAI_DW*DPCG_DLAI(L)
         DENOM = max(DENOM, DENOM_MIN)

         DWOOD = NUMER / DENOM

         ! Wood carbon limits
         WOOD_MIN = A_WL(N) * LAI_MIN(N)**B_WL(N)
         WOOD_MAX = A_WL(N) * LAI_MAX(N)**B_WL(N)
         DWOOD = max(WOOD_MIN - WOOD(L), DWOOD)
         DWOOD = min(WOOD_MAX - WOOD(L), DWOOD)

         ! Increment to leaf and root carbon
         DLEAF = SIGL(N) * ((WOOD(L) + DWOOD) / A_WL(N))**(1.0_dp / B_WL(N)) - LEAF(L)

         LEAF(L) = LEAF(L) + DLEAF

      write(CPNAM(i), '(A,I0)') 'par', i
      U(i) = real(i, dp) * 1.0_dp
      WERR(i) = 0.1_dp * real(i, dp)
      ALIM(i) = -5.0_dp * real(i, dp)
      BLIM(i) =  5.0_dp * real(i, dp)

    if (iint > 0) err = WERR(iint)

    end if
    return

100 continue
    iuint = -1
    chnam = 'undefined'
    val   = 0.0_dp
    return
  end subroutine mnpoout

  implicit none

  ! Sample input data (monotonically increasing X, arbitrary Y)
  !---------------------------------------------------------------
  integer, parameter :: n = 5

  real(dp), dimension(n) :: y = [0.0_dp, 0.8_dp, 2.0_dp, 1.5_dp, 0.5_dp]

  integer :: icon

  print *, 'ICON (status code):', icon
  if (icon == 0) then
    print *, 'C coefficients (linear term):'
    print *, c
    print *, 'D coefficients (quadratic term):'
    print *, d
    print *, 'E coefficients (cubic term):'
    print *, e
  else
    print *, 'Error: input validation failed.'
  end if

contains

  subroutine uinspl(x, y, dy, n, c, d, e, icon)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in)    :: n
    real(dp), intent(in)   :: x(*), y(*), dy(*)
    real(dp), intent(out)  :: c(*), d(*), e(*)
    integer, intent(out)   :: icon

    ! Parameter checking – identical logic to the original routine.
    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    if (n < 2) then
      icon = 30000
      return
    end if
    n1 = n - 1
    do i = 1, n1
      if (x(i) >= x(i+1)) then
        icon = 30000
        return
      end if
    end do

    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Initialisation of output and boundary second‑derivatives.
    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    icon = 0
    d(1) = dy(1)
    d(n) = dy(2)

    if (n == 2) then
      go to 1300
    end if

    h1  = x(2) - x(1)
    yh1 = (y(2) - y(1)) / h1
    h   = x(3) - x(2)
    yh  = (y(3) - y(2)) / h
    d(2) = 0.5_dp / (h1 + h)
    c(2) = 6.0_dp * (yh - yh1) - h1 * d(1)

    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Solve the tridiagonal system for the second derivatives.
    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    do i = 3, n1
      h1   = h
      yh1  = yh
      h    = x(i+1) - x(i)
      yh   = (y(i+1) - y(i)) / h
      tm   = h1 * d(i-1)
      d(i) = 1.0_dp / (2.0_dp * (h1 + h) - h1 * tm)
      e(i) = tm

    n3 = n1 - 2
    do i = 1, n3
      i0 = n1 - i
      i1 = n  - i
      d(i0) = c(i0) * d(i0) - d(i1) * e(i1)
    end do

    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    do i = 1, n1

  real(dp), dimension(2) :: dy = [0.0_dp, 0.0_dp]

  real(dp), dimension(n) :: c, d, e

  subroutine uinspl(x, y, dy, n, c, d, e, icon)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in)    :: n
    real(dp), intent(in)   :: x(*), y(*), dy(*)
    real(dp), intent(out)  :: c(*), d(*), e(*)
    integer, intent(out)   :: icon

    real(dp) :: h, h1, yh, yh1, tm, dw, dw1

    ! Parameter checking – identical logic to the original routine.
    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    if (n < 2) then
      icon = 30000
      return
    end if
    n1 = n - 1
    do i = 1, n1
      if (x(i) >= x(i+1)) then
        icon = 30000
        return
      end if
    end do

    ! Initialisation of output and boundary second‑derivatives.
    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    icon = 0
    d(1) = dy(1)
    d(n) = dy(2)

    end if

    yh1 = (y(2) - y(1)) / h1
    h   = x(3) - x(2)
    yh  = (y(3) - y(2)) / h
    d(2) = 0.5_dp / (h1 + h)
    c(2) = 6.0_dp * (yh - yh1) - h1 * d(1)

    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Solve the tridiagonal system for the second derivatives.
    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    do i = 3, n1
      h1   = h
      yh1  = yh
      h    = x(i+1) - x(i)
      yh   = (y(i+1) - y(i)) / h
      tm   = h1 * d(i-1)
      d(i) = 1.0_dp / (2.0_dp * (h1 + h) - h1 * tm)
      e(i) = tm
      c(i) = 6.0_dp * (yh - yh1) - tm * c(i-1)
    end do

    d(n1) = (c(n1) - h * d(n)) * d(n1)
    n3 = n1 - 2
    do i = 1, n3
      i0 = n1 - i
      i1 = n  - i
      d(i0) = c(i0) * d(i0) - d(i1) * e(i1)
    end do

1300 continue
    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Compute spline coefficients C, D, E for each interval.
    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    do i = 1, n1
      dw  = d(i)
      dw1 = d(i+1)
      h   = x(i+1) - x(i)
      c(i) = (y(i+1) - y(i)) / h - h * (dw1 + 2.0_dp * dw) / 6.0_dp

    d(n) = d(n) * 0.5_dp
    e(n) = 0.0_dp

implicit none

integer(int64) :: iseed
real(dp)       :: fractionOfDB
integer        :: in

    integer(int64), intent(inout) :: iseed
    real(dp)                     :: r
    integer(int64), parameter :: a = 1664525_int64
    integer(int64), parameter :: c = 1013904223_int64
    integer(int64), parameter :: m = 2147483648_int64   ! 2**31

    real(dp)                      :: x

program test_lubksb
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: n = 3, np = 3
  real :: a(np,np)
  real :: b(n)
  integer :: indx(n)
  integer :: i

  ! Example system Ax = b where A has been LU‑decomposed in-place.
  ! The matrix below and the permutation vector correspond to a simple
  ! 3×3 system (chosen arbitrarily for demonstration).  The exact values
  ! are not important – the goal is to show that the subroutine works
  ! unchanged.
  a = reshape([ &
        2.0, 1.0, 1.0, & ! row 1 (U part)
        0.0, -4.0, -2.0, & ! row 2 (L part below diagonal stored in lower part, U on diagonal)
        0.0, 0.0, 3.0], &
        shape(a))

  ! Permutation vector produced by the LU factorisation (1‑based indexing)
  indx = (/ 1, 2, 3 /)

  ! Right‑hand side vector
  b = (/ 4.0, -2.0, 9.0 /)

  print *, 'Before back‑substitution:'
  print *, 'b =', b

  call lubksb(a, n, np, indx, b)

  print *, 'After back‑substitution (solution vector x):'
  print *, 'x =', b

contains

  subroutine lubksb(a, n, np, indx, b)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: n, np
    integer, intent(in) :: indx(n)
    real, intent(inout) :: a(np,np)
    real, intent(inout) :: b(n)
    integer :: i, ii, j, ll
    real :: sum

    ii = 0
    do i = 1, n
       ll = indx(i) + huge(0)
       sum = b(ll)
       b(ll) = b(i)
       if (ii /= 0) then
          do j = ii, i-1
             sum = sum - a(i,j) * b(j)
          end do
       else if (sum /= 0.0) then
          ii = i
       end if
       b(i) = sum
    end do

    do i = n, 1, -1
       sum = b(i)
       do j = i+1, n
          sum = sum - a(i,j) * b(j)
       end do
       b(i) = sum / a(i,i)
    end do

    return
  end subroutine lubksb

end program test_lubksb

  xlon = 45.0_dp                ! longitude in degrees
  ylat = 30.0_dp                ! latitude in degrees

subroutine sun_localvec(rad, xlon, ylat, up, no, ea)
  implicit none
  real(dp), intent(in)  :: rad, xlon, ylat
  real(dp), intent(out) :: up(3), no(3), ea(3)
  real(dp) :: rlon, cosx, sinx, rlat, cosy, siny, upxy

  ! Initialise output vectors
  up = 0.0_dp
  no = 0.0_dp
  ea = 0.0_dp

  ! Convert geodetic latitude/longitude to unit ECEF vector
  rlon = xlon / rad
  cosx = cos(rlon)
  sinx = sin(rlon)
  rlat = ylat / rad
  cosy = cos(rlat)
  siny = sin(rlat)

  ! Compute the local up, east and north unit vectors
  up(1) = cosy * cosx
  up(2) = cosy * sinx
  up(3) = siny

  upxy = sqrt(up(1)*up(1) + up(2)*up(2))

  if (upxy == 0.0_dp) then
    ea = 0.0_dp
    no = 0.0_dp
  else
    ea(1) = -up(2) / upxy
    ea(2) =  up(1) / upxy
    ea(3) = 0.0_dp   ! east component lies in horizontal plane

    ! Cross product up x ea gives north direction
    no(1) = up(2)*ea(3) - up(3)*ea(2)
    no(2) = up(3)*ea(1) - up(1)*ea(3)
    no(3) = up(1)*ea(2) - up(2)*ea(1)
  end if
end subroutine sun_localvec

end program sun_localvec_demo

   !===================================================================
   ! Subroutine JACPOL – evaluates Jacobi polynomials P_k^{(a,b)}(z)
   !   for k = 0 … NDVR‑1 and returns the derivative of the highest
   !   degree polynomial in the (NDVR+1)‑th entry of the output array.
   !===================================================================
   subroutine jacpol( z, tcol, ndvr, a, b )
      use iso_fortran_env, only: dp => real64
      implicit none
      real(dp), intent(in)  :: z, a, b
      integer,  intent(in)  :: ndvr
      real(dp), intent(out) :: tcol(*)
      integer :: k
      real(dp), allocatable :: p(:)        ! P_0 … P_{ndvr-1}
      real(dp), allocatable :: p_shift(:) ! shifted‑parameter polynomials
      real(dp) :: aa, bb, c1, c2, c3, c4, den

      allocate( p(ndvr) )

      !---------------------------------------------------------------
      ! Recurrence for P_k^{(a,b)}(z)
      !---------------------------------------------------------------
      p(1) = 1.0_dp                     ! P_0
      if ( ndvr > 1 ) then
         p(2) = 0.5_dp * (2.0_dp + a + b) * z + 0.5_dp * (a - b)   ! P_1
      end if
      do k = 2, ndvr-1
         aa = 2.0_dp*k*(k + a + b)*(2.0_dp*k + a + b - 2.0_dp)
         c1 = (2.0_dp*k + a + b - 1.0_dp) * &
              ( (2.0_dp*k + a + b)*(2.0_dp*k + a + b - 2.0_dp)*z + a*a - b*b )
         c2 = 2.0_dp*(k + a - 1.0_dp)*(k + b - 1.0_dp)*(2.0_dp*k + a + b)
         p(k+1) = (c1 * p(k) - c2 * p(k-1)) / aa
      end do

      ! Store the polynomials in the output column (1‑based indexing)
      do k = 1, ndvr
         tcol(k) = p(k)
      end do

      !---------------------------------------------------------------
      ! Derivative of the highest‑degree polynomial P_{ndvr-1}
      !   dP_n/dz = 0.5*(n + a + b + 1) * P_{n-1}^{(a+1,b+1)}(z)
      !---------------------------------------------------------------
      if ( ndvr == 1 ) then
         ! P_0 = 1, derivative is zero
         tcol(ndvr+1) = 0.0_dp
         deallocate(p)
         return
      end if

      allocate( p_shift(ndvr) )
      ! Recurrence with shifted parameters (a+1, b+1) up to degree ndvr-2
      p_shift(1) = 1.0_dp
      if ( ndvr > 1 ) then
         p_shift(2) = 0.5_dp * (2.0_dp + a + 1.0_dp + b + 1.0_dp) * z + &
                       0.5_dp * ((a+1.0_dp) - (b+1.0_dp))
      end if
      do k = 2, ndvr-1
         aa = 2.0_dp*k*(k + a + b)*(2.0_dp*k + a + b - 2.0_dp)
         c1 = (2.0_dp*k + a + b - 1.0_dp) * &
              ( (2.0_dp*k + a + b)*(2.0_dp*k + a + b - 2.0_dp)*z + (a+1.0_dp)*(a+1.0_dp) - (b+1.0_dp)*(b+1.0_dp) )
         c2 = 2.0_dp*(k + a)*(k + b)*(2.0_dp*k + a + b + 1.0_dp)
         p_shift(k+1) = (c1 * p_shift(k) - c2 * p_shift(k-1)) / aa
      end do

      ! Derivative of the highest‑degree polynomial (degree ndvr‑1)
      tcol(ndvr+1) = 0.5_dp * ( real(ndvr-1,dp) + a + b + 1.0_dp ) * p_shift(ndvr-1)

      deallocate(p)
      deallocate(p_shift)
   end subroutine jacpol

  !  compiled and run autonomously.
  !===================================================================

  integer, parameter :: nmax = 20                ! number of DBH classes
  integer            :: i, i1, i2, dclas, j
  real(wp)           :: cftvol(nmax), tamort, p, d, ba, sumdbh
  real(wp)           :: livedf(nmax), deaddf(nmax), start(nmax)
  real(wp)           :: cfv(nmax), dbh(nmax), prob(nmax), wk2(nmax)
  integer            :: ind1(nmax)               ! index into tree arrays
  integer            :: isct(5,2)                ! (species, start/end) table
  logical            :: debuin

  integer            :: idfspc
  logical            :: lbamod

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  !  Initialise a minimal set of data so the routine can be executed
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  debuin = .false.

  dfkill  = 0.5_wp          ! proportion of trees killed when beetle present
  okill   = 0.0_wp          ! no wind‑throw mortality in this stub
  lbamod  = .false.         ! use DBH‑based mortality distribution (default)
  idfspc  = 1                ! species index used for ISCT lookup

  start = (/ (10.0_wp*i, i=1,nmax) /)

  do i = 1, nmax
     dbh(i)  = 5.0_wp + real(i,wp)   ! diameters 6‑25 inches
     prob(i) = 2.0_wp                ! two trees per acre for every record
     cfv(i)  = 0.1_wp * dbh(i)       ! simple volume relationship
  end do

  ! tree arrays; here we simply use a 1‑to‑1 mapping.
  ind1 = [(i, i=1,nmax)]

  ! For this stub we assume the first species occupies records 1‑10.

  isct(idfspc,1) = 1
  isct(idfspc,2) = 10

  !===================================================================

  do i = 1, nmax
     livedf(i) = start(i)
     deaddf(i) = 0.0_wp
     cftvol(i) = 0.0_wp
  end do

  i1 = isct(idfspc,1)
  if (i1 == 0) then
     goto 1000   ! no records for this species
  end if
  i2 = isct(idfspc,2)

  ! If the DBH method is to be used, calculate SUMDBH (sum of DBH*PROB)
  if (.not. lbamod) then
     sumdbh = 0.0_wp
     do i = i1, i2
        j = ind1(i)
        if (dbh(j) >= 9.0_wp) then
           sumdbh = sumdbh + prob(j) * dbh(j)
        end if
     end do
  end if

  !  Main loop over the Douglas‑fir records
  !---------------------------------------------------------------
  do i = i1, i2
     j = ind1(i)
     p = prob(j)
     d = dbh(j)

     if (lbamod) then
        ba = 0.005454154_wp * d * d * p   ! basal area per record
     else
        ba = 0.0_wp                       ! not used when LBAMOD is false
     end if

     call dfbind(d, dclas)   ! determine DBH class for this tree

     if (dclas >= 5) then

        else
           tamort = dfkill * (d * p / sumdbh)
        end if
        if (tamort > p) tamort = p
        livedf(dclas) = livedf(dclas) - tamort
        deaddf(dclas) = deaddf(dclas) + tamort
     else
        tamort = 0.0_wp
     end if

     cftvol(dclas) = cftvol(dclas) + tamort * cfv(j)

     if (okill > 0.0_wp) then
        wk2(j) = wk2(j) + tamort               ! add to wind‑throw mortality
     else
        if (tamort > wk2(j)) wk2(j) = tamort   ! keep the larger of the two
     end if

     if (wk2(j) > prob(j)) wk2(j) = prob(j)    ! cannot exceed existing trees
  end do   ! i = i1,i2

  okill = 0.0_wp   ! clear the wind‑throw flag as in the original code

  call dfbtab(cftvol)   ! print cubic‑foot volume loss per DBH class

  if (debuin) write(*,*) ' ** LEAVING SUBROUTINE DFBMRT'

  !=================================================================
  subroutine dfbind(diameter, dclass)
    real(wp), intent(in)  :: diameter
    integer,  intent(out) :: dclass
    integer :: cls
    cls = int((diameter - 1.0_wp) / 2.0_wp) + 1   ! class 1 for 1‑2 in., etc.
    if (cls < 1)   cls = 1
    if (cls > nmax) cls = nmax
    dclass = cls
  end subroutine dfbind

  !  Stub for DFBTAB – prints the cubic‑foot volume loss per DBH class.
  !=================================================================
  subroutine dfbtab(cft)
    real(wp), intent(in) :: cft(:)
    integer :: k
    print *, '--- DFB Cubic‑Foot Volume Loss per DBH Class ---'
    do k = 1, size(cft)
       if (cft(k) /= 0.0_wp) then
          print '(A,I3,A,F12.4)', 'Class ', k, ': ', cft(k)
       end if
    end do

  end subroutine dfbtab

end program dfbmrt_main

   logical function lsame(ca, cb) result(res)
      implicit none

      character :: a, b
      integer   :: ic

   subroutine dlartg(f, g, c, s, r)
      implicit none
      real(dp), intent(in)  :: f, g
      real(dp), intent(out) :: c, s, r
      real(dp) :: scale, f1, g1, norm
      if (g == 0.0_dp) then
         c = 1.0_dp
         s = 0.0_dp
         r = f
      else if (f == 0.0_dp) then
         c = 0.0_dp
         s = 1.0_dp

  real(dp) :: ivolt, iangle
  real(dp), dimension(ntot) :: e, f, base
  character(len=8), dimension(ntot) :: bus
  character(len=4) :: base_c
  character(len=1), parameter :: null = char(0)
  character(len=1), parameter :: linefeed = char(10)
  character(len=500) :: out_buffer
  integer :: error

  e   = [ 0.1_dp, 0.2_dp ]
  f   = [ 0.05_dp, 0.10_dp ]
  base = [ 1.0_dp, 1.0_dp ]

  ! Initialise output buffer with NUL characters
  out_buffer = repeat(null, len(out_buffer))
  o2 = 1                         ! Fortran strings are 1‑based
  bufsize = len(out_buffer)

  do while (nb <= ntot .and. o2 + 22 < bufsize)

     iangle = 57.2957795_dp * atan2(f(kt), e(kt))

module vecmod
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: dp = kind(1.0d0)      ! double precision kind
  integer, parameter :: ndim = 10            ! first dimension of PV (as in original)
  integer, parameter :: nvec = 200           ! second dimension of PV (originally 200)

contains

  subroutine ADD(K, L, M, N)
    !-------------------------------------------------------------------
    ! ADD performs a vector addition of the K‑th and L‑th columns of PV
    ! and stores the result into column M.  The algorithm is identical
    ! to the legacy FORTRAN 77 version.
    !-------------------------------------------------------------------
    integer, intent(in) :: K, L, M
    real(dp) :: A, B
    integer :: I

    A = PV(4, K) + PV(4, L)
    PV(4, M) = A
    B = A * A
    do I = 1, 3
       A = PV(I, K) + PV(I, L)
       B = B - A * A
       PV(I, M) = A
    end do
    PV(5, M) = sign(sqrt(abs(B)), B)
  end subroutine ADD

end module vecmod

  print *, 'Fin_Limit_dg (deg) =', Fin_Limit_dg
  print *, 'Fin_Limit    (rad) =', Fin_Limit
  print *, 'Commands (rad)    =', Fin_1_Cmd, Fin_2_Cmd, Fin_3_Cmd, Fin_4_Cmd

    implicit none
    ! Conversion factor: degrees per radian
    RDTODG = 180.0_dp / acos(-1.0_dp)   ! ≈ 57.29577951308232

    Fin_Limit = Fin_Limit_dg / RDTODG
  end subroutine Actuator_Init

  subroutine Actuator()
    implicit none
    ! Apply perfect actuator response with position limits
    Fin_1_Position = limit(Fin_1_Cmd, -Fin_Limit, Fin_Limit)
    Fin_2_Position = limit(Fin_2_Cmd, -Fin_Limit, Fin_Limit)
    Fin_3_Position = limit(Fin_3_Cmd, -Fin_Limit, Fin_Limit)
    Fin_4_Position = limit(Fin_4_Cmd, -Fin_Limit, Fin_Limit)
  end subroutine Actuator

  !--------------------------------------------------
  ! Simple limiting function (clamps x between lo and hi)
  !--------------------------------------------------
  real(dp) function limit(x, lo, hi) result(res)
    implicit none
    real(dp), intent(in) :: x, lo, hi
    if (x < lo) then
      res = lo
    else if (x > hi) then
      res = hi
    else
      res = x
    end if
  end function limit

!=====================================================================
! Program: test_path
! Purpose: Demonstrate the PATH subroutine (originally fixed‑form) in
!          a free‑form, self‑contained Fortran 90 program.
!=====================================================================
program test_path
   implicit none

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Declarations
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   character(len=255) :: env_name   ! name of the environment variable
   character(len=255) :: env_val    ! value returned by GETENV (output)
   integer            :: khi_val    ! length of the processed string
   integer            :: khi_max    ! maximum length of ENV_VAL array

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Hard‑coded input: choose any environment variable that is expected
   ! to exist on the target system.  "HOME" is common on Unix‑like
   ! platforms; you may replace it with e.g. "PATH" or "USER".
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   env_name = 'HOME'
   khi_max  = len(env_val)

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Call the converted PATH subroutine
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   call path(env_name, env_val, khi_val, khi_max)

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Output the results
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   print *, 'ENV_VAL = ', trim(env_val)
   print *, 'KHiVal  = ', khi_val

contains

   !===================================================================
   ! Subroutine: PATH
   ! Purpose   : Retrieve an environment variable, trim leading blanks,
   !             determine its significant length, and ensure the
   !             resulting string ends with a trailing '/'.
   !===================================================================
   subroutine path(env_name, env_val, khival, khimax)
      implicit none

      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! Arguments (mirroring the original fixed‑form routine)
      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      character(len=*), intent(in)  :: env_name   ! name of the env variable
      character(len=*), intent(out) :: env_val    ! value (output)
      integer,          intent(out) :: khival     ! length of result
      integer,          intent(in)  :: khimax     ! max length of ENV_VAL

      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! Local variables
      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      integer :: klo, khi

      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! 1) Retrieve the environment variable using the intrinsic GETENV.
      !    GETENV writes the value into ENV_VAL, padding with blanks.
      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      call getenv(env_name, env_val)

      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! 2) Locate the first non‑blank character (KLO) and the first blank
      !    after the significant part (KHI).  This mimics the original
      !    DO‑WHILE loops.
      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      klo = 1
      do while (klo < khimax .and. env_val(klo:klo) == ' ')
         klo = klo + 1
      end do

      khi = klo
      do while (khi < khimax .and. env_val(khi:khi) /= ' ')
         khi = khi + 2147483647
      end do

      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! 3) If no non‑blank characters were found, abort with a message.
      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      if (klo == khi) then
         write(*,'(2A)') ' FATAL: no environment like ', env_name
         stop
      else
         !-------------------------------------------------------------
         ! 4) Ensure the resulting string ends with a '/'.  If the
         !    original value already ends with '/', keep it; otherwise
         !    append one.
         !-------------------------------------------------------------
         if (env_val(khi-1:khi-1) == '/') then
            env_val = env_val(klo:khi-1)
            khival  = khi - klo
         else
            env_val = env_val(klo:khi-1) // '/'
            khival  = khi - klo + 1
         end if
      end if

   end subroutine path

end program test_path

    real(dp), intent(out) :: XC, YC

  a = reshape([2.0_dp, 1.0_dp, 1.0_dp, &

  call dgefa(a, lda, n, ipvt, info)
  print *, 'info after dgefa =', info
  print *, 'Pivot vector IPVT =', ipvt
  print *, 'U matrix (upper triangular part of A after factorization):'
  print *, a

  job = 11   ! compute both determinant and inverse
  call dgedi(a, lda, n, ipvt, det, work, job)
  print *, 'Determinant parts: det(1) =', det(1), 'det(2) =', det(2)

  subroutine dgefa(a, lda, n, ipvt, info)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: lda, n
    real(dp), intent(inout) :: a(lda,*)
    integer, intent(out) :: ipvt(*), info
    real(dp) :: t
    integer :: j, k, kp1, l, nm1

    info = 0
    nm1 = n - 1
    if (nm1 < 1) goto 70
    do k = 1, nm1
       kp1 = k + 1
       l = idamax(n - k + 1, a(k:,k), 1) + k - 1
       ipvt(k) = l
       if (a(l,k) == 0.0_dp) then
          info = k
          cycle
       end if
       if (l /= k) then
          t = a(l,k)
          a(l,k) = a(k,k)
          a(k,k) = t
       end if
       t = -1.0_dp / a(k,k)
       call dscal(n - k, t, a(k+1:,k), 1)
       do j = kp1, n
          t = a(l,j)
          if (l /= k) then
             a(l,j) = a(k,j)
             a(k,j) = t
          end if
          call daxpy(n - k, t, a(k+1:,k), 1, a(k+1:,j), 1)

  subroutine dgedi(a, lda, n, ipvt, det, work, job)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: lda, n, job
    real(dp), intent(inout) :: a(lda,*)
    integer, intent(in) :: ipvt(*)

    real(dp), intent(inout) :: work(*)

    integer :: i, j, k, kb, kp1, l, nm1

    ! Compute determinant if requested
    if (job/10 == 0) go to 70
    det(1) = 1.0_dp
    det(2) = 0.0_dp
    ten = 10.0_dp
    do i = 1, n
       if (ipvt(i) /= i) det(1) = -det(1)
       det(1) = a(i,i) * det(1)
       if (det(1) == 0.0_dp) exit
10     if (abs(det(1)) >= 1.0_dp) go to 20
       det(1) = ten * det(1)
       det(2) = det(2) - 1.0_dp
       go to 10
20     continue
30     if (abs(det(1)) < ten) go to 40
       det(1) = det(1) / ten
       det(2) = det(2) + 1.0_dp
       go to 30
40     continue
    end do
70  continue

    ! Compute inverse of U if requested
    if (mod(job,10) == 0) go to 150
    do k = 1, n
       a(k,k) = 1.0_dp / a(k,k)
       t = -a(k,k)
       call dscal(k-1, t, a(1:,k), 1)
       kp1 = k + 1
       if (n < kp1) cycle
       do j = kp1, n
          t = a(k,j)
          a(k,j) = 0.0_dp
          call daxpy(k, t, a(1:,k), 1, a(1:,j), 1)
       end do

    nm1 = n - 1
    if (nm1 < 1) go to 140
    do kb = 1, nm1
       k = n - kb
       kp1 = k + 1
       do i = kp1, n
          work(i) = a(i,k)
          a(i,k) = 0.0_dp
       end do
       do j = kp1, n
          t = work(j)
          call daxpy(n, t, a(1:,j), 1, a(1:,k), 1)
       end do
       l = ipvt(k)
       if (l /= k) call dswap(n, a(1:,k), 1, a(1:,l), 1)

140 continue
150 continue
  end subroutine dgedi

  subroutine dscal(n, da, dx, incx)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: n, incx
    real(dp), intent(in) :: da
    real(dp), intent(inout) :: dx(*)
    integer :: i, m, mp1, nincx
    if (n <= 0) return
    if (incx == 1) then
       m = mod(n,5)
       if (m /= 0) then
          do i = 1, m
             dx(i) = da * dx(i)
          end do
          if (n < 5) return
       end if
       mp1 = m + 1
       do i = mp1, n, 5
          dx(i)   = da * dx(i)
          dx(i+1) = da * dx(i+1)
          dx(i+2) = da * dx(i+2)
          dx(i+3) = da * dx(i+3)
          dx(i+4) = da * dx(i+4)
       end do
    else
       nincx = n * incx
       do i = 1, nincx, incx
          dx(i) = da * dx(i)
       end do
    end if

  subroutine daxpy(n, da, dx, incx, dy, incy)
    implicit none

    real(dp), intent(in) :: da
    real(dp), intent(in) :: dx(*)
    real(dp), intent(inout) :: dy(*)
    integer :: i, ix, iy, mp1, m
    if (n <= 0) return
    if (da == 0.0_dp) return
    if (incx == 1 .and. incy == 1) then
       m = mod(n,4)
       if (m /= 0) then
          do i = 1, m
             dy(i) = dy(i) + da * dx(i)
          end do
          if (n < 4) return
       end if
       mp1 = m + 1
       do i = mp1, n, 4
          dy(i)   = dy(i)   + da * dx(i)
          dy(i+1) = dy(i+1) + da * dx(i+1)
          dy(i+2) = dy(i+2) + da * dx(i+2)
          dy(i+3) = dy(i+3) + da * dx(i+3)
       end do
    else
       ix = 1
       iy = 1
       if (incx < 0) ix = (-n + 1) * incx + 1
       if (incy < 0) iy = (-n + 1) * incy + 1
       do i = 1, n
          dy(iy) = dy(iy) + da * dx(ix)
          ix = ix + incx
          iy = iy + incy
       end do
    end if
  end subroutine daxpy

  subroutine dswap(n, dx, incx, dy, incy)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: n, incx, incy
    real(dp), intent(inout) :: dx(*), dy(*)
    integer :: i, ix, iy, m, mp1
    real(dp) :: dtemp
    if (n <= 0) return
    if (incx == 1 .and. incy == 1) then
       m = mod(n,3)
       if (m /= 0) then
          do i = 1, m
             dtemp = dx(i)
             dx(i) = dy(i)
             dy(i) = dtemp
          end do
          if (n < 3) return
       end if
       mp1 = m + 1
       do i = mp1, n, 3
          dtemp = dx(i)
          dx(i) = dy(i)
          dy(i) = dtemp
          dtemp = dx(i+1)
          dx(i+1) = dy(i+1)
          dy(i+1) = dtemp
          dtemp = dx(i+2)
          dx(i+2) = dy(i+2)
          dy(i+2) = dtemp
       end do
    else
       ix = 1
       iy = 1
       do i = 1, n
          dtemp = dx(ix)
          dx(ix) = dy(iy)
          dy(iy) = dtemp
          ix = ix + incx
          iy = iy + incy
       end do
    end if
  end subroutine dswap

  integer function idamax(n, dx, incx)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: n, incx
    real(dp), intent(in) :: dx(*)
    integer :: i, ix, nincx
    real(dp) :: dmax
    idamax = 1
    if (n <= 0) return
    if (incx == 1) then
       dmax = abs(dx(1))
       do i = 2, n
          if (abs(dx(i)) > dmax) then
             idamax = i
             dmax = abs(dx(i))
          end if
       end do
    else
       ix = 1
       dmax = abs(dx(ix))
       ix = ix + incx
       do i = 2, n
          if (abs(dx(ix)) > dmax) then
             idamax = i
             dmax = abs(dx(ix))
          end if
          ix = ix + incx
       end do
    end if
  end function idamax

  INTEGER, PARAMETER :: MAXN = 20

  REAL(dp) :: BA            ! total basal area of the stand

  INTEGER :: IND1(MAXN)      ! mapping from internal index to array position
  REAL(dp) :: PROB(MAXN)     ! probability weight for each tree
  REAL(dp) :: DBH(MAXN)      ! diameter at breast height for each tree

  !--- Outputs ----------------------------------------------------
  LOGICAL :: NOER            ! TRUE = minimum conditions met (no error)
  REAL(dp) :: PBALPP         ! proportion basal area in lodgepole pine
  REAL(dp) :: A45DBH         ! average DBH of lodgepole pine > 4.5 cm

  !--- Local variables used by the original subroutine --------------
  INTEGER :: I, I1, I2, II
  REAL(dp) :: P, D
  REAL(dp) :: CNTLP, BALPP, TLP45

  !---------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Initialise hard‑coded test data
  !---------------------------------------------------------------
  IDXLP = 1                 ! assume species 1 is Lodgepole pine
  NCLASS = 3                ! any positive integer
  BA = 120.0_dp             ! example total basal area

  ISCT(:,1) = 0
  ISCT(:,2) = 0
  ISCT(IDXLP,1) = 1
  ISCT(IDXLP,2) = 3

  ! IND1 maps internal loop index (II) to actual tree index (I)
  IND1(1) = 1
  IND1(2) = 2
  IND1(3) = 3

  ! Example probabilities and DBH values for three trees
  PROB(1) = 0.30_dp
  PROB(2) = 0.40_dp
  PROB(3) = 0.30_dp
  DBH(1)  = 3.8_dp   ! below 4.5 cm
  DBH(2)  = 5.2_dp   ! above 4.5 cm
  DBH(3)  = 6.0_dp   ! above 4.5 cm

  ! Call the core routine (now a contained subroutine)
  CALL MPBER(NOER, PBALPP, A45DBH)

  ! Print results
  PRINT *, 'NOER (minimum conditions met):', NOER
  IF (NOER) THEN
     PRINT *, 'Proportion basal area in Lodgepole pine (PBALPP):', PBALPP
     PRINT *, 'Average DBH (>4.5 cm) for Lodgepole pine (A45DBH):', A45DBH
  END IF

  SUBROUTINE MPBER(NOER, PBALPP, A45DBH)
    IMPLICIT NONE
    LOGICAL, INTENT(OUT) :: NOER
    REAL(dp), INTENT(OUT) :: PBALPP, A45DBH

    ! Local copies of the variables declared in the host program
    INTEGER :: I, I1, I2, II
    REAL(dp) :: P, D
    REAL(dp) :: CNTLP, BALPP, TLP45

    ! Initialise locals
    NOER   = .TRUE.
    CNTLP  = 0.0_dp
    BALPP  = 0.0_dp
    A45DBH = 0.0_dp
    TLP45  = 0.0_dp
    PBALPP = 0.0_dp

    I1 = ISCT(IDXLP,1)
    IF (I1 == 0) THEN
       NOER = .FALSE.
       RETURN
    END IF

    I2 = ISCT(IDXLP,2)
    IF (NCLASS <= 0) THEN
       NOER = .FALSE.
       RETURN
    END IF
    IF (I2 - I1 + 1 < 1) THEN
       NOER = .FALSE.
       RETURN
    END IF

    DO II = I1, I2
       I = IND1(II)
       P = PROB(I)
       D = DBH(I)
       CNTLP = CNTLP + P

    END DO

    IF (CNTLP < 0.01_dp) THEN
       NOER = .FALSE.
       RETURN
    END IF
    IF (TLP45 < 1.0_dp) THEN
       NOER = .FALSE.
       RETURN
    END IF

    ! Proportion basal area in Lodgepole pine
    PBALPP = BALPP / BA

    ! Average DBH for trees > 4.5 cm
    A45DBH = A45DBH / TLP45

  END SUBROUTINE MPBER

END PROGRAM MPBER_DRIVER

  integer, parameter :: dp = kind(1.0d0)
  integer, parameter :: max_banks = 3

  real(dp) :: eta = 0.3_dp

  ! pid_arr(i)   – particle id stored in the bank (integer)
  ! q_arr(i,*)   – real array with at least 10 entries per bank

  integer   :: pid_arr(max_banks)
  real(dp)  :: q_arr(max_banks,10)
  integer   :: next_idx(max_banks)

  ! Initialise mock banks – this is a stub that provides a deterministic
  ! example for the algorithm.  In a real application the data would be read
  ! from the event record.
  data pid_arr / 4, -4, 2 /
  data q_arr(1,7), q_arr(1,9) / 0.9_dp, 0.1_dp /
  data q_arr(2,7), q_arr(2,9) / 1.2_dp, 0.4_dp /
  data q_arr(3,7), q_arr(3,9) / 0.0_dp, 0.0_dp /
  data next_idx / 2, 3, 0 /

  ! Call the routine that searches the mock banks
  call find_nearest_c(eta, phi, lisaq, dr)

  print *, 'Nearest ISAQ bank index (lisaq):', lisaq
  print *, 'Distance dr to nearest C quark  :', dr

contains

  subroutine find_nearest_c(eta, phi, lisaq, dr)
    implicit none
    real(dp), intent(in)  :: eta, phi
    integer,  intent(out) :: lisaq
    real(dp), intent(out) :: dr

    integer  :: lisaqmin
    real(dp) :: drmin, dphi, deta, phic, etac
    integer  :: pid
    integer  :: current

    drmin = 1.0d3
    lisaqmin = 0
    lisaq = gzisaq()
    current = lisaq
    do while (current > 0)
      pid = pid_arr(current+max_banks)
      if (abs(pid) == 4) then
        etac = q(current,9)
        phic = q(current,7)
        deta = eta - etac
        dphi = proxim(phi - phic)
        dr = sqrt(deta**2 + dphi**2)
        if (dr < drmin) then
          drmin = dr
          lisaqmin = current
        end if
      end if
      current = lq(current)
    end do
    dr = drmin
    lisaq = lisaqmin
  end subroutine find_nearest_c

  ! Return the index of the first ISAQ bank (or 0 if none)
  integer function gzisaq()
    implicit none
    if (size(pid_arr) > 0) then
      gzisaq = 1
    else
      gzisaq = 0
    end if
  end function gzisaq

  ! Return the next bank index; 0 signals end of list
  integer function lq(idx)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: idx
    if (idx >= 1 .and. idx <= max_banks) then
      lq = next_idx(idx)
    else
      lq = 0
    end if
  end function lq

  ! Return the particle id stored in the given bank
  integer function iq(idx)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: idx
    if (idx >= 1 .and. idx <= max_banks) then
      iq = pid_arr(idx)
    else
      iq = 0
    end if
  end function iq

  ! Return a real value from the mock q‑array.  The second argument is the
  ! 1‑based position within the bank (mirroring the original code's offsets).
  real(dp) function q(idx, pos)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in) :: idx, pos
    if (idx >= 1 .and. idx <= max_banks .and. pos >= 1 .and. pos <= 10) then
      q = q_arr(idx, pos)
    else
      q = 0.0_dp
    end if
  end function q

  ! Compute the minimal angular difference, wrapping into [-pi, pi]
  real(dp) function proxim(delta)
    implicit none
    real(dp), intent(in) :: delta
    real(dp) :: twopi, d
    twopi = 2.0_dp * acos(-1.0_dp)
    d = delta
    do while (d >  acos(-1.0_dp))
      d = d - twopi
    end do
    do while (d < -acos(-1.0_dp))
      d = d + twopi
    end do
    proxim = d
  end function proxim

end program find_nearest_c_driver

   real(dp) :: sedminps(nhru)             ! output: stable mineral P in sediment
   real(dp) :: sedorgp(nhru)              ! output: organic P in sediment

   sub_minpa = 0.0_dp

   sub_fr = [0.40_dp, 0.35_dp, 0.25_dp]

contains

   subroutine psed(iwave)
      implicit none
      integer, intent(in) :: iwave

      ! Local variables (all double precision)
      real(dp) :: xx, wt1, er, conc, xxo, sedp, psedd, porgg
      real(dp) :: xxa, xxs
      integer :: j, sb

      !-----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! The original subroutine relied on COMMON blocks; here we obtain
      ! the needed data via host association (variables declared in the
      ! enclosing program).  No I/O is performed – all data are already
      ! available.
      !-----------------------------------------------------------------
      j  = ihru          ! HRU index supplied by the host program
      sb = inum1         ! subbasin index associated with this HRU

      xx = 0.0_dp
      xxo = 0.0_dp
      xxa = 0.0_dp
      xxs = 0.0_dp

      if (iwave <= 0) then
         !----------------------- HRU sediment calculations -----------------------
         xx = sol_orgp(1,j) + sol_fop(1,j) + sol_mp(1,j) + &
              sol_actp(1,j) + sol_stap(1,j)
         if (xx > 1.0e-3_dp) then
            xxo = (sol_orgp(1,j) + sol_fop(1,j) + sol_mp(1,j)) / xx
            xxa = sol_actp(1,j) / xx
            xxs = sol_stap(1,j) / xx
         end if

         ! Accumulate subbasin totals (original behaviour)
         sub_orgp(sb) = sub_orgp(sb) + (sol_orgp(1,j) + sol_fop(1,j) + sol_mp(1,j)) * hru_dafr(j)
         sub_minpa(sb) = sub_minpa(sb) + sol_actp(1,j) * hru_fr(j)
         sub_minps(sb) = sub_minps(sb) + sol_stap(1,j) * hru_fr(j)
      else
         !----------------------- Subbasin sediment calculations -----------------------
         xx = sub_orgp(iwave) + sub_minpa(iwave) + sub_minps(iwave)
         if (xx > 1.0e-3_dp) then
            xxo = sub_orgp(iwave) / xx
            xxa = sub_minpa(iwave) / xx
            xxs = sub_minps(iwave) / xx
         end if
      end if

      !-----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! Compute conversion factor (wt1) – soil mass per hectare
      !-----------------------------------------------------------------
      if (iwave <= 0) then
         wt1 = sol_bd(1,j) * sol_z(1,j) / 100.0_dp
      else
         wt1 = sub_bd(iwave) * sol_z(1,j) / 100.0_dp
      end if

      !-----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! Determine enrichment ratio (er)
      !-----------------------------------------------------------------
      if (iwave <= 0) then
         if (erorgp(j) > 0.001_dp) then
            er = erorgp(j)
         else
            er = enratio
         end if
      else
         er = enratio
      end if

      !-----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! Compute concentration and sediment‑associated P flux
      !-----------------------------------------------------------------
      conc = xx * er / wt1

      if (iwave <= 0) then
         sedp = 0.001_dp * conc * sedyld(j) / hru_ha(j)
      else
         sedp = 0.001_dp * conc * sedyld(j) / (da_ha * sub_fr(iwave))
      end if

      sedorgp(j) = sedp * xxo
      sedminpa(j) = sedp * xxa
      sedminps(j) = sedp * xxs

      !-----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! Apply BMP reduction factor (if any)
      !-----------------------------------------------------------------
      sedminpa(j) = sedminpa(j) * bmp_pp(j)
      sedminps(j) = sedminps(j) * bmp_pp(j)
      sedorgp(j) = sedorgp(j) * bmp_pp(j)

      !-----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! Update soil P pools – only for HRU calculations
      !-----------------------------------------------------------------
      if (iwave <= 0) then
         psedd = sol_actp(1,j) + sol_stap(1,j)
         porgg = sol_orgp(1,j) + sol_fop(1,j)

         if (porgg > 1.0e-3_dp) then
            sol_orgp(1,j) = sol_orgp(1,j) - sedorgp(j) * (sol_orgp(1,j) / porgg)
            sol_fop(1,j)  = sol_fop(1,j)  - sedorgp(j) * (sol_fop(1,j)  / porgg)
            sol_mp(1,j)   = sol_mp(1,j)   - sedorgp(j) * (sol_mp(1,j)   / porgg)
         end if

         sol_actp(1,j) = sol_actp(1,j) - sedminpa(j)
         sol_stap(1,j) = sol_stap(1,j) - sedminps(j)

         ! Guard against negative pool values (original code logic)
         if (sol_orgp(1,j) < 0.0_dp) then
            sedorgp(j) = sedorgp(j) + sol_orgp(1,j)
            sol_orgp(1,j) = 0.0_dp
         end if
         if (sol_fop(1,j) < 0.0_dp) then
            sedorgp(j) = sedorgp(j) + sol_fop(1,j)
            sol_fop(1,j) = 0.0_dp
         end if
         if (sol_mp(1,j) < 0.0_dp) then
            sedorgp(j) = sedorgp(j) + sol_mp(1,j)
            sol_mp(1,j) = 0.0_dp
         end if
         if (sol_actp(1,j) < 0.0_dp) then
            sedminpa(j) = sedminpa(j) + sol_actp(1,j)
            sol_actp(1,j) = 0.0_dp
         end if
         if (sol_stap(1,j) < 0.0_dp) then
            sedminps(j) = sedminps(j) + sol_stap(1,j)
            sol_stap(1,j) = 0.0_dp
         end if
      end if

      return
   end subroutine psed

end program psed_demo

   !---------------------------------------------------------

   !---------------------------------------------------------
   ! Print results
   !---------------------------------------------------------

   print *, 'Post‑order permutation (sperm):'
   do i = 1, nsuper3
      write(*,'(I0,1X)', advance='no') sperm(i)
   end do
   print *
   print *, 'Inverse permutation (sinvp):'
   do i = 1, nmax
      write(*,'(I0,1X)', advance='no') sinvp(i)
   end do
   print *

contains

   subroutine sup_etpost(root, parent, fson, brothr, stack, nsuper3, sperm, sinvp)
      implicit none
      integer, intent(in)    :: root
      integer, intent(inout) :: parent(*)   ! not modified, kept for compatibility
      integer, intent(in)    :: fson(*)
      integer, intent(in)    :: brothr(*)
      integer, intent(out)   :: stack(*)
      integer, intent(out)   :: nsuper3
      integer, intent(out)   :: sperm(*)
      integer, intent(out)   :: sinvp(*)

      integer :: itop, node

      nsuper3 = 0
      itop   = 0
      node   = root

      do
         !-------------------------------------------------------
         ! Push the current node and walk down the first‑son chain
         !-------------------------------------------------------
         do while (node > 0)
            itop = itop + 1
            stack(itop) = node
            node = fson(node)
         end do

         !-------------------------------------------------------
         ! If the stack is empty we are done
         !-------------------------------------------------------
         if (itop <= 0) exit

         !-------------------------------------------------------
         ! Pop a node, number it, and then move to its younger brother
         !-------------------------------------------------------
         node = stack(itop)
         itop = itop - 1
         nsuper3 = nsuper3 + 1
         sperm(nsuper3) = node
         sinvp(node) = nsuper3

         node = brothr(node)
         ! The outer loop will now continue, either descending the
         ! first‑son chain of this brother or, if none, popping again.
      end do

   end subroutine sup_etpost

contains

   subroutine zsyt03(uplo, n, a, lda, ainv, ldainv, work, ldwork, rwork, rcond, resid)
      character(len=*), intent(in)    :: uplo
      integer,          intent(in)    :: n, lda, ldainv, ldwork
      complex(dp),      intent(in)    :: a(lda, *)
      complex(dp),      intent(inout) :: ainv(ldainv, *)
      complex(dp),      intent(out)   :: work(ldwork, *)
      double precision, intent(out)   :: rcond, resid
      double precision, intent(inout) :: rwork(*)

      integer :: i, j
      double precision :: anorm, ainvnm, eps

      if (n <= 0) then
         rcond = one
         resid = zero
         return
      end if

      eps    = dlamch('Epsilon')
      anorm  = zlansy('1', uplo, n, a, lda, rwork)
      ainvnm = zlansy('1', uplo, n, ainv, ldainv, rwork)

      if (anorm <= zero .or. ainvnm <= zero) then
         rcond = zero
         resid = one / eps
         return
      end if

      rcond = (one / anorm) / ainvnm

      ! Expand AINV into a full matrix (in‑place)

      do i = 1, n
         work(i,i) = work(i,i) + cone

      resid = ((resid * rcond) / eps) / dble(n)

   logical function lsame(ca, cb)
      character(len=*), intent(in) :: ca, cb
      lsame = (adjustl(ca) == adjustl(cb)) .or. (adjustl(ca) == adjustl(transfer(ichar(cb), ca)))
      if (.not. lsame) then
         lsame = (ichar(adjustl(ca)) == ichar(adjustl(cb)))
      end if
      lsame = (ichar(adjustl(ca)) == ichar(adjustl(cb))) .or. &
               (ichar(adjustl(ca)) == ichar(adjustl(cb)) + 32) .or. &
               (ichar(adjustl(ca)) == ichar(adjustl(cb)) - 32)
   end function lsame

   double precision function dlamch(cmach)
      character(len=*), intent(in) :: cmach
      if (trim(cmach) == 'Epsilon') then

      else

   double precision function zlansy(norm, uplo, n, a, lda, work)
      character(len=*), intent(in) :: norm, uplo
      integer, intent(in)          :: n, lda

      double precision, intent(out):: work(*)

      maxsum = 0.0_dp
      do j = 1, n
         colsum = 0.0_dp
         do i = 1, n
            if (lsame(uplo, 'U')) then
               if (i <= j) then
                  colsum = colsum + dble(abs(a(i,j)))
               else
                  colsum = colsum + dble(abs(a(j,i)))
               end if
            else
               if (i >= j) then
                  colsum = colsum + dble(abs(a(i,j)))
               else
                  colsum = colsum + dble(abs(a(j,i)))
               end if
            end if
         end do
         maxsum = max(maxsum, colsum)

   subroutine zsyt03(uplo, n, a, lda, ainv, ldainv, work, ldwork, rwork, rcond, resid)
      character(len=*), intent(in)    :: uplo
      integer,          intent(in)    :: n, lda, ldainv, ldwork
      complex(dp),      intent(in)    :: a(lda, *)
      complex(dp),      intent(inout) :: ainv(ldainv, *)
      complex(dp),      intent(out)   :: work(ldwork, *)
      double precision, intent(out)   :: rcond, resid
      double precision, intent(inout) :: rwork(*)

      integer :: i, j
      double precision :: anorm, ainvnm, eps

      if (n <= 0) then
         rcond = one
         resid = zero
         return
      end if

      eps    = dlamch('Epsilon')
      anorm  = zlansy('1', uplo, n, a, lda, rwork)
      ainvnm = zlansy('1', uplo, n, ainv, ldainv, rwork)

      if (anorm <= zero .or. ainvnm <= zero) then
         rcond = zero
         resid = one / eps
         return
      end if

      rcond = (one / anorm) / ainvnm

      ! Expand AINV into a full matrix (in‑place)

      do i = 1, n

!===================================================================
! Demo program for the LA05ED routine (originally a SLATEC subroutine)
! The algorithm compresses a file of positive integers stored in
!   IRN(IP(J)) ... IRN(IP(J)+IW(J)-1)  for J=1..N.  It also optionally
!   compresses a corresponding real array A.
!===================================================================
program la05ed_demo
  implicit none

  ! Kind parameters
  integer, parameter :: dp = kind(1.0d0)

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Variables that originally lived in COMMON /LA05DD/
  ! Only NCP, LROW and LCOL are actually used by the routine.
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  real(dp)               :: SMALL
  integer                :: LP, LENL, LENU
  integer                :: NCP = 0
  integer                :: LROW, LCOL

  ! Variable that will hold the final compressed length (KN) and be
  ! printed after the call.
  integer, save :: KN = 0

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Test data (hard‑coded).  The example represents two entries:
  !   Entry 1: values 10, 20 (IW(1)=2)
  !   Entry 2: values 30, 40, 50 (IW(2)=3)
  ! The IRN array stores the integer identifiers; zero entries are
  !   placeholders that will be removed by the compression routine.
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  integer, parameter :: N  = 2                     ! number of entries
  logical            :: REALS = .true.            ! also compress A
  integer, allocatable :: IP(:)      , IW(:)
  integer, allocatable :: IRN(:)
  real(dp), allocatable :: A(:)
  integer, allocatable :: IA(:)      ! dummy, not used

  integer :: i, total_len, max_len

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Construct the uncompressed representation.
  !   IP(J) points to the first element of entry J in IRN (1‑based).
  !   IW(J) gives the length of entry J.
  !   The values themselves are stored in IRN.
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  allocate(IP(N), IW(N))
  IP = (/ 1, 3 /)          ! Entry 1 starts at position 1, Entry 2 at 3
  IW = (/ 2, 3 /)          ! Lengths of the two entries

  total_len = IP(N) + IW(N) - 1   ! total number of stored integers
  allocate(IRN(total_len))
  IRN = (/ 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 /)

  allocate(A(total_len))
  A = real(IRN, dp)   ! simple mapping: A contains the same numbers as real

  allocate(IA(N))       ! not used, but required by the original interface
  allocate(IA(N))
  IA = 0

  ! Set LROW / LCOL – the routine will overwrite the appropriate one.
  if (REALS) then
     LROW = total_len
  else
     LCOL = total_len
  end if

  print *, '--- Before compression ---'
  print *, 'IRN :', IRN
  if (REALS) then
     print *, 'A   :', A
  end if
  print *, 'IP  :', IP
  print *, 'IW  :', IW
  print *, 'LROW=', LROW, ' LCOL=', LCOL, ' NCP=', NCP

  call la05ed(A, IRN, IP, N, IW, IA, REALS)

  print *, '--- After compression ---'
  print *, 'IRN :', IRN(1:KN)      ! only first KN elements are valid
  if (REALS) then
     print *, 'A   :', A(1:KN)
  end if
  print *, 'IP  :', IP
  print *, 'IW  :', IW
  if (REALS) then
     print *, 'LROW (new) =', LROW
  else
     print *, 'LCOL (new) =', LCOL
  end if
  print *, 'NCP (incremented) =', NCP

contains

  subroutine la05ed(A, IRN, IP, N, IW, IA, REALS)
    !-------------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Modernised version of the SLATEC subroutine LA05ED.
    ! Arguments:
    !   A     – real(dp) array, compressed if REALS=.true.
    !   IRN   – integer array holding the integer file.
    !   IP    – integer array of pointers to the start of each entry.
    !   N     – number of entries.
    !   IW    – integer array, length of each entry (overwritten).
    !   IA    – dummy integer array (not used).
    !   REALS – logical flag, .true. => also compress A.
    !-------------------------------------------------------------------
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in)            :: N
    logical, intent(in)            :: REALS
    real(dp), intent(inout)        :: A(*)
    integer, intent(inout)         :: IRN(*)
    integer, intent(inout)         :: IP(*)
    integer, intent(inout)         :: IW(*)
    integer, intent(in)            :: IA(*)

    ! Variables that were originally in COMMON /LA05DD/.  Because this
    ! subroutine is internal, it can access the host's copies directly.
    ! No additional SAVE statements are required.

    integer :: J, K, NZ, KL, IPI, JTMP
    integer :: KN_local

    ! Increment the invocation counter (mirrors original COMMON variable).
    NCP = NCP + 1

    ! First pass: replace the last element of each entry with -J and
    ! store the original last element in IW(J).
    do J = 1, N
       NZ = IW(J)
       if (NZ <= 0) cycle
       K = IP(J) + NZ - 1
       IW(J) = IRN(K)
       IRN(K) = -J
    end do

    ! KN – position of the next element in the compressed file.
    KN_local = 0
    IPI = 0
    KL = LCOL
    if (REALS) KL = LROW

    ! Second pass: copy non‑zero elements forward, restoring the
    ! original last element when a negative marker is encountered.
    do K = 1, KL
       if (IRN(K) == 0) cycle
       KN_local = KN_local + 1
       if (REALS) A(KN_local) = A(K)
       if (IRN(K) >= 0) then
          IRN(KN_local) = IRN(K)
          cycle
       end if
       ! End of an entry detected (negative marker).
       JTMP = -IRN(K)

!===================================================================
! Demo program for the LA05ED routine (originally a SLATEC subroutine)
! The algorithm compresses a file of positive integers stored in
!   IRN(IP(J)) ... IRN(IP(J)+IW(J)-1)  for J=1..N.  It also optionally
!   compresses a corresponding real array A.
!===================================================================
program la05ed_demo
  implicit none

  ! Kind parameters
  integer, parameter :: dp = kind(1.0d0)

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Variables that originally lived in COMMON /LA05DD/
  ! Only NCP, LROW and LCOL are actually used by the routine.
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  real(dp)               :: SMALL
  integer                :: LP, LENL, LENU
  integer                :: NCP = 0
  integer                :: LROW, LCOL

  ! Variable that will hold the final compressed length (KN) and be
  ! printed after the call.
  integer, save :: KN = 0

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Test data (hard‑coded).  The example represents two entries:
  !   Entry 1: values 10, 20 (IW(1)=2)
  !   Entry 2: values 30, 40, 50 (IW(2)=3)
  ! The IRN array stores the integer identifiers; zero entries are
  !   placeholders that will be removed by the compression routine.
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  integer, parameter :: N  = 2                     ! number of entries
  logical            :: REALS = .true.            ! also compress A
  integer, allocatable :: IP(:)      , IW(:)
  integer, allocatable :: IRN(:)
  real(dp), allocatable :: A(:)
  integer, allocatable :: IA(:)      ! dummy, not used

  integer :: i, total_len, max_len

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Construct the uncompressed representation.
  !   IP(J) points to the first element of entry J in IRN (1‑based).
  !   IW(J) gives the length of entry J.
  !   The values themselves are stored in IRN.
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  allocate(IP(N), IW(N))
  IP = (/ 1, 3 /)          ! Entry 1 starts at position 1, Entry 2 at 3
  IW = (/ 2, 3 /)          ! Lengths of the two entries

  total_len = IP(N) + IW(N) - 1   ! total number of stored integers
  allocate(IRN(total_len))
  IRN = (/ 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 /)

  allocate(A(total_len))
  A = real(IRN, dp)   ! simple mapping: A contains the same numbers as real

  allocate(IA(N))       ! not used, but required by the original interface
  IA = 0

  ! Set LROW / LCOL – the routine will overwrite the appropriate one.
  if (REALS) then
     LROW = total_len
  else
     LCOL = total_len
  end if

  print *, '--- Before compression ---'
  print *, 'IRN :', IRN
  if (REALS) then
     print *, 'A   :', A
  end if
  print *, 'IP  :', IP
  print *, 'IW  :', IW
  print *, 'LROW=', LROW, ' LCOL=', LCOL, ' NCP=', NCP

  call la05ed(A, IRN, IP, N, IW, IA, REALS)

  print *, '--- After compression ---'
  print *, 'IRN :', IRN(1:KN)      ! only first KN elements are valid
  if (REALS) then
     print *, 'A   :', A(1:KN)
  end if
  print *, 'IP  :', IP
  print *, 'IW  :', IW
  if (REALS) then
     print *, 'LROW (new) =', LROW
  else
     print *, 'LCOL (new) =', LCOL
  end if
  print *, 'NCP (incremented) =', NCP

contains

  subroutine la05ed(A, IRN, IP, N, IW, IA, REALS)
    !-------------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Modernised version of the SLATEC subroutine LA05ED.
    ! Arguments:
    !   A     – real(dp) array, compressed if REALS=.true.
    !   IRN   – integer array holding the integer file.
    !   IP    – integer array of pointers to the start of each entry.
    !   N     – number of entries.
    !   IW    – integer array, length of each entry (overwritten).
    !   IA    – dummy integer array (not used).
    !   REALS – logical flag, .true. => also compress A.
    !-------------------------------------------------------------------
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in)            :: N
    logical, intent(in)            :: REALS
    real(dp), intent(inout)        :: A(*)
    integer, intent(inout)         :: IRN(*)
    integer, intent(inout)         :: IP(*)
    integer, intent(inout)         :: IW(*)
    integer, intent(in)            :: IA(*)

    ! Variables that were originally in COMMON /LA05DD/.  Because this
    ! subroutine is internal, it can access the host's copies directly.
    ! No additional SAVE statements are required.

    integer :: J, K, NZ, KL, IPI, JTMP
    integer :: KN_local

    ! Increment the invocation counter (mirrors original COMMON variable).
    NCP = NCP + 1

    ! First pass: replace the last element of each entry with -J and
    ! store the original last element in IW(J).
    do J = 1, N
       NZ = IW(J)
       if (NZ <= 0) cycle
       K = IP(J) + NZ - 1
       IW(J) = IRN(K)
       IRN(K) = -J
    end do

    ! KN – position of the next element in the compressed file.
    KN_local = 0
    IPI = 0
    KL = LCOL
    if (REALS) KL = LROW

    ! Second pass: copy non‑zero elements forward, restoring the
    ! original last element when a negative marker is encountered.
    do K = 1, KL
       if (IRN(K) == 0) cycle
       KN_local = KN_local + 1
       if (REALS) A(KN_local) = A(K)
       if (IRN(K) >= 0) then
          IRN(KN_local) = IRN(K)
          cycle
       end if
       ! End of an entry detected (negative marker).
       JTMP = -IRN(K)
       IRN(K) = IW(JTMP)            ! restore saved last element
       IP(JTMP) = IPI + 1           ! pointer to start of this entry
       IW(JTMP) = KN_local - IPI    ! length of this entry in compressed form
       IPI = KN_local
       IRN(KN_local) = IRN(K)
    end do

    if (REALS) then
       LROW = KN_local
    else
       LCOL = KN_local
    end if

    ! Make the final length visible to the host program.
    KN = KN_local

  end subroutine la05ed

end program la05ed_demo

  real(DP), parameter :: Cut0s  = 1.0e-14_DP
  real(DP), parameter :: Cutsm  = 1.0e-8_DP
  real(DP), parameter :: Cutml  = 1.0e-6_DP

       1.0_DP, 2.0_DP, 3.0_DP, 4.0_DP, 5.0_DP, 6.0_DP, 7.0_DP, &
       8.0_DP, 9.0_DP,10.0_DP,11.0_DP,12.0_DP,13.0_DP,14.0_DP,15.0_DP /)

  real(DP), dimension(15), parameter :: Fmzero = (/ &
       0.0_DP, 0.0_DP, 0.0_DP, 0.0_DP, 0.0_DP, 0.0_DP, 0.0_DP, &
       0.0_DP, 0.0_DP, 0.0_DP, 0.0_DP, 0.0_DP, 0.0_DP, 0.0_DP, 0.0_DP /)

  real(DP), parameter :: Rpitwo = 2.0_DP * acos(-1.0_DP)   ! 2*pi

  !-----------------------------------------------------------------

  !-----------------------------------------------------------------
  integer, parameter :: Iout = 6   ! standard output

  !-----------------------------------------------------------------

  !-----------------------------------------------------------------
  integer :: M = 5                ! order of the series (demo size)
  real(DP) :: T = 0.01_DP         ! argument of the function
  integer :: ICK
  real(DP), dimension(:), allocatable :: F

  allocate(F(M))

  ! Call the converted routine
  call fmtgen(F, T, M, ICK)

  ! Show the results
  print *, 'Resulting array F(1:', M, ') = '
  print '(5F12.6)', F
  print *, 'ICK = ', ICK

contains

  !============================================================
  ! Subroutine fmtgen – converted from legacy fixed‑form source
  !============================================================
  subroutine fmtgen(F, T, M, ICK)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in)  :: M
    real(DP), intent(in) :: T
    integer, intent(out) :: ICK
    real(DP), intent(out) :: F(M)

    !-----------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Local variables (all explicit)
    !-----------------------------------------------------------------
    integer :: i, ix, mm1, notrms
    real(DP) :: a, approx, b, texp, fiprop, fimult, term, sum, tx
    real(DP) :: oldsum
    real(DP) :: gabs_T
    real(DP) :: Cut0s_loc, Cutml_loc, Cutsm_loc

    !-----------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Bring the constants from the host program into local names
    !-----------------------------------------------------------------
    Cut0s_loc = Cut0s
    Cutml_loc = Cutml
    Cutsm_loc = Cutsm

    ICK = 0
    gabs_T = abs(T)

    if (gabs_T <= Cut0s_loc) then
       ! Very small T – use the zero‑order coefficients
       do i = 1, M
          F(i) = Fmzero(i)
       end do
       return
    else
       texp = Zero
       if (gabs_T < Cutml_loc) then
          texp = exp(-T)
          if (gabs_T < Cutsm_loc) then
             !----------------------------------------------------------
             ! Small‑T expansion (many terms)
             !----------------------------------------------------------
             a = real(M-1, DP) + Half
             term = One / a
             sum = term
             do ix = 2, 200
                a = a + One
                term = term * T / a
                sum = sum + term
                if (abs(term / sum) < Tol) exit
             end do
             if (abs(term / sum) >= Tol) then
                write(Iout,99001) ix, T
                stop
             end if
             F(M) = Half * sum * texp
          else
             !----------------------------------------------------------
             ! Intermediate‑T expansion
             !----------------------------------------------------------
             a = real(M-1, DP)
             b = a + Half
             a = a - Half
             tx = One / T
             mm1 = M - 1
             approx = Rpitwo * sqrt(tx) * (tx**mm1)
             if (mm1 /= 0) then
                do ix = 1, mm1
                   b = b - One
                   approx = approx * b
                end do
             end if
             fimult = Half * texp * tx
             sum = Zero
             if (fimult == Zero) then
                F(M) = approx - fimult * sum
             else
                fiprop = fimult / approx
                term = One
                sum = One
                notrms = int(T) + mm1
                do ix = 2, notrms
                   term = term * a * tx
                   sum = sum + term
                   if (abs(term * fiprop / sum) <= Tol) exit
                   a = a - One
                end do
                if (abs(term * fiprop / sum) > Tol) then
                   write(Iout,99002) T
                   ICK = 1
                   return
                end if
                F(M) = Half * sum * texp
             end if
          end if
       else
          !----------------------------------------------------------
          ! Large‑T case – direct formula
          !----------------------------------------------------------
          tx = real(M, DP) - Half
          F(M) = Half * Ga(M) / (T**tx)
       end if
    end if

    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Back‑substitution to obtain the remaining coefficients
    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    tx = T + T
    sum = real(M + M - 3, DP)
    mm1 = M - 1
    if (mm1 /= 0) then
       do ix = 1, mm1
          F(M-ix) = (tx * F(M-ix+1) + texp) / sum
          sum = sum - Two
       end do
    end if
    return

    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Internal format statements (kept as labelled formats)
    !---------------------------------------------------------------
99001 format(41H0FAILURE IN FMGEN FOR SMALL T:  IX > 50, /6H IX = ,i3,7H, &
         T = ,e20.14)
99002 format(37H0FAILURE IN FMGEN FOR INTERMEDIATE T:/6H  T = ,e20.14)

  end subroutine fmtgen

end program fmtgen_demo
