module fpm_error
   use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only : stdin=>input_unit, stdout=>output_unit, stderr=>error_unit
   implicit none
   private

   public :: error_t
   public :: fatal_error, syntax_error, file_not_found_error
   public :: file_parse_error, bad_name_error, fpm_stop

   !> Data type defining an error
   type :: error_t
      character(len=:), allocatable :: message
   end type error_t

contains

   !> Generic fatal runtime error
   subroutine fatal_error(error, message)
      type(error_t), allocatable, intent(out) :: error
      character(len=*), intent(in)            :: message
      allocate(error)
      error%message = message
   end subroutine fatal_error

   subroutine syntax_error(error, message)
      type(error_t), allocatable, intent(out) :: error
      character(len=*), intent(in)            :: message
      allocate(error)
      error%message = message
   end subroutine syntax_error

   !> Checks a name and, if invalid, creates an error object.
   function bad_name_error(error, label, name) result(is_bad)
      type(error_t), allocatable, intent(out) :: error
      character(len=*), intent(in)            :: label
      character(len=*), intent(in)            :: name
      logical                                 :: is_bad

      if (.not. is_fortran_name(to_fortran_name(name))) then
         is_bad = .true.
         allocate(error)
         error%message = 'manifest file syntax error: '//label// &
                          ' name must be composed only of alphanumerics, "-" and "_"  and start with a letter ::'//name
      else
         is_bad = .false.
      end if
   end function bad_name_error

   !> Error created when a file is missing or not found
   subroutine file_not_found_error(error, file_name)
      type(error_t), allocatable, intent(out) :: error
      character(len=*), intent(in)            :: file_name
      allocate(error)
      error%message = "'"//file_name//"' could not be found, check if the file exists"
   end subroutine file_not_found_error

   !> Error created when file parsing fails
   subroutine file_parse_error(error, file_name, message, line_num, line_string, line_col)
      type(error_t), allocatable, intent(out) :: error
      character(len=*), intent(in)            :: file_name
      character(len=*), intent(in)            :: message
      integer, intent(in), optional           :: line_num
      character(len=*), intent(in), optional :: line_string
      integer, intent(in), optional           :: line_col

      character(50) :: temp_string

      allocate(error)
      error%message = 'Parse error: '//message//new_line('a')
      error%message = error%message//file_name

      if (present(line_num)) then
         write(temp_string,'(I0)') line_num
         error%message = error%message//':'//trim(temp_string)
      end if

      if (present(line_col)) then
         if (line_col > 0) then
            write(temp_string,'(I0)') line_col
            error%message = error%message//':'//trim(temp_string)
         end if
      end if

      if (present(line_string)) then
         error%message = error%message//new_line('a')
         error%message = error%message//'   | '//line_string
         if (present(line_col)) then
            if (line_col > 0) then
               error%message = error%message//new_line('a')
               error%message = error%message//'   | '//repeat(' ',line_col-1)//'^'
            end if
         end if
      end if
   end subroutine file_parse_error

   subroutine fpm_stop(value, message)
      integer, intent(in)            :: value
      character(len=*), intent(in)   :: message
      integer                         :: iostat
      if (message /= '') then
         flush(unit=stderr, iostat=iostat)
         flush(unit=stdout, iostat=iostat)
         if (value > 0) then
            write(stderr,'("<ERROR> ",a)') trim(message)
         else
            write(stderr,'("<INFO> ",a)') trim(message)
         end if
         flush(unit=stderr, iostat=iostat)
      end if

   function is_fortran_name(name) result(res)
      character(len=*), intent(in) :: name
      logical                      :: res
      integer                       :: i, n
      character                     :: c
      n = len_trim(name)
      if (n == 0) then
         res = .false.
         return
      end if
      c = name(1:1)
      if (.not. ((c >= 'A' .and. c <= 'Z') .or. (c >= 'a' .and. c <= 'z'))) then
         res = .false.
         return
      end if
      do i = 2, n
         c = name(i:i)
         select case (c)
         case ('A':'Z','a':'z','0':'9','-','_')
            cycle
         case default
            res = .false.
            return
         end select
      end do
      res = .true.

   function to_fortran_name(name) result(res)
      character(len=*), intent(in) :: name

   end function to_fortran_name

    end do
  end subroutine print_complex_matrix

    implicit none

    character(len=12) :: str
    write(str,'(i0)') i
  end function itoa

    ! Compute helicity amplitudes for a heavy quark–gluon system.
    implicit none
    real(dp), intent(in)    :: mq
    integer, intent(in)     :: ig, is, ie, in, it
    complex(dp), intent(out):: amp(2,2)
    real(dp)                :: prop
    integer :: i, j

    prop = sqrt( ( dble( za(ie,in) * zb(in,ie) ) - wmss**2 )**2 &

    !--- Helicity amplitudes ---------------------------------------------------
    amp(1,2) = za(ie,it) / ( za(ig,is) * za(ig,it) ) * &

    amp(2,2) = -mq / za(ig,it) * za(ig,ie) / ( za(ig,is) * za(ig,it) ) * &

    do i = 1, 2

    real(kind=SP), dimension(:), intent(in) :: x, y

    ax = sum(x) / real(n, kind=SP)
    ay = sum(y) / real(n, kind=SP)
    xt = x - ax
    yt = y - ay

    syy = dot_product(yt, yt)
    sxy = dot_product(xt, yt)

  hcode%nch      = 2

  hcode%iright(1) = 0
  hcode%iright(2) = 0

  call hufdec(ich, nb, code, hcode)

    ! Simple Cooley‑Tukey FFT (radix‑2, in‑place) for power‑of‑two lengths
    complex(sp), intent(inout) :: data(:)
    integer, intent(in)        :: isign
    integer                    :: n, i, j, m, mmax, istep
    real(sp)                   :: theta, wtemp, wr, wi, wpr, wpi
    complex(sp)                :: w, tempr
    n = size(data)
    !--- bit‑reversal permutation ---
    j = 1
    do i = 1, n
       if (j > i) then
          tempr = data(j)
          data(j) = data(i)
          data(i) = tempr
       end if
       m = n/2
       do while ( (m >= 1) .and. (j > m) )
          j = j - m
          m = m/2
       end do
       j = j + m
    end do

       theta = real(isign,sp) * 2.0_sp * acos(-1.0_sp) / real(mmax,sp)
       wtemp = sin(0.5_sp*theta)
       wpr   = -2.0_sp * wtemp * wtemp

          wr = wr*wpr - wi*wpi + wr

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   subroutine sort2(a, b)
      real(sp), intent(inout) :: a(:), b(:)

      real(sp) :: atemp, btemp
      n = size(a)

         c = 1.0_sp + aa / c

!=====================================================================
!  Hard‑coded implementation of the original NR "spear" routine
!  with all dependencies supplied locally.  Compiles with:
!    gfortran -O0 -ffree-line-length-none -w spear_fixed.f90

module nr_mod
   use iso_fortran_env, only: real32, int32
   implicit none
   integer, parameter :: sp = real32   ! single‑precision kind
   integer, parameter :: i4b = int32   ! 4‑byte integer kind

contains

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Simple equality assertion used in the original code
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   integer function assert_eq(a, b, msg) result(res)
      integer, intent(in) :: a, b
      character(*), intent(in) :: msg
      if (a /= b) then
         print *, 'ASSERTION FAILED: ', trim(msg), ': ', a, ' /= ', b
         stop 1
      end if
      res = a
   end function assert_eq

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Sort two parallel arrays (ascending order of a, permuting b)
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   subroutine sort2(a, b)
      real(sp), intent(inout) :: a(:), b(:)
      integer :: i, j, n
      real(sp) :: atemp, btemp
      n = size(a)
      do i = 2, n
         atemp = a(i)
         btemp = b(i)
         j = i - 1
         do while (j >= 1 .and. a(j) > atemp)
            a(j+1) = a(j)
            b(j+1) = b(j)
            j = j - 1
         end do
         a(j+1) = atemp
         b(j+1) = btemp
      end do
   end subroutine sort2

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Arithmetic progression – used for ranking in "crank"
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   function arth(start, step, n) result(arr)
      integer, intent(in) :: start, step, n
      integer, allocatable :: arr(:)
      integer :: i
      allocate(arr(n))
      do i = 1, n
         arr(i) = start + (i-1)*step
      end do
   end function arth

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Simple copy routine – mimics the NR utility
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   subroutine array_copy(src, dest, n, ndum)
      integer(i4b), intent(in)  :: src(:)
      integer(i4b), intent(out) :: dest(:)
      integer(i4b), intent(out) :: n, ndum
      n = size(src)
      dest(1:n) = src
      ndum = 0
   end subroutine array_copy

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Continued‑fraction evaluation of the incomplete beta function
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   function betacf(a, b, x) result(cf)
      real(sp), intent(in) :: a, b, x
      real(sp) :: cf
      integer, parameter :: MAXIT = 100
      real(sp), parameter :: EPS = 1.0e-7_sp, FPMIN = 1.0e-30_sp
      integer :: m, m2
      real(sp) :: aa, c, d, del, h, qab, qap, qam

      qab = a + b
      qap = a + 1.0_sp
      qam = a - 1.0_sp
      c = 1.0_sp
      d = 1.0_sp - qab * x / qap
      if (abs(d) < FPMIN) d = FPMIN
      d = 1.0_sp / d
      h = d

      do m = 1, MAXIT
         m2 = 2 * m
         aa = real(m,sp) * (b - real(m,sp)) * x / &
              ((qam + real(m2,sp)) * (a + real(m2,sp)))
         d = 1.0_sp + aa * d
         if (abs(d) < FPMIN) d = FPMIN
         c = 1.0_sp + aa / c
         if (abs(c) < FPMIN) c = FPMIN
         d = 1.0_sp / d
         h = h * d * c

         aa = - (a + real(m,sp)) * (qab + real(m,sp)) * x / &
               ((a + real(m2,sp)) * (qap + real(m2,sp)))
         d = 1.0_sp + aa * d
         if (abs(d) < FPMIN) d = FPMIN
         c = 1.0_sp + aa / c
         if (abs(c) < FPMIN) c = FPMIN
         d = 1.0_sp / d
         del = d * c
         h = h * del
         if (abs(del - 1.0_sp) < EPS) exit
      end do
      cf = h
   end function betacf

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------

      real(sp), intent(in) :: a, b, x
      real(sp) :: res
      real(sp) :: bt
      if (x < 0.0_sp .or. x > 1.0_sp) then
         print *, 'betai: x out of range', x
         stop 1
      end if
      if (x == 0.0_sp .or. x == 1.0_sp) then
         res = 0.0_sp
         return
      end if
      bt = exp( log(gamma(a+b)) - log(gamma(a)) - log(gamma(b)) + &
                a*log(x) + b*log(1.0_sp - x) )
      if (x < (a+1.0_sp)/(a+b+2.0_sp)) then
         res = bt * betacf(a, b, x) / a
      else
         res = 1.0_sp - bt * betacf(b, a, 1.0_sp - x) / b
      end if
   end function betai

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Complementary error function – simply the intrinsic "erfc"
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   function erfcc(x) result(res)
      real(sp), intent(in) :: x
      real(sp) :: res
      res = erfc(x)
   end function erfcc

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Compute the "crank" statistic used in the Spearman rank test
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   subroutine crank(w, s)
      real(sp), intent(inout) :: w(:)
      real(sp), intent(out)   :: s
      integer(i4b) :: n, i, nties, ndum
      integer(i4b), allocatable :: tstart(:), tend(:), tie(:), idx(:)

      n = size(w)
      allocate(idx(n))
      allocate(tie(n))
      idx = arth(1, 1, n)
      tie = merge(1, 0, w == eoshift(w, -1))
      tie(1) = 0
      w = real(idx, sp)   ! replace values by their ranks

      if (all(tie == 0)) then
         s = 0.0_sp
         deallocate(idx, tie)
         return
      end if

      allocate(tstart(n), tend(n))
      call array_copy(pack(idx, tie < eoshift(tie, 1)), tstart, nties, ndum)
      tend(1:nties) = pack(idx, tie > eoshift(tie, 1))

      do i = 1, nties
         w(tstart(i):tend(i)) = real((tstart(i) + tend(i))/2, sp)
      end do

      tend(1:nties) = tend(1:nties) - tstart(1:nties) + 1
      s = sum(tend(1:nties)**3 - tend(1:nties))

      deallocate(idx, tie, tstart, tend)
   end subroutine crank

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   !  Main Spearman rank‑correlation routine (original "spear")
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   subroutine spear(data1, data2, d, zd, probd, rs, probrs)
      real(sp), intent(in)  :: data1(:), data2(:)
      real(sp), intent(out) :: d, zd, probd, rs, probrs
      integer(i4b)          :: n
      real(sp)               :: aved, df, en, en3n, fac, sf, sg, t, vard
      real(sp), allocatable  :: wksp1(:), wksp2(:)

      n = assert_eq(size(data1), size(data2), 'spear')
      allocate(wksp1(n))
      allocate(wksp2(n))
      wksp1 = data1
      wksp2 = data2

      call sort2(wksp1, wksp2)
      call crank(wksp1, sf)
      call sort2(wksp2, wksp1)   ! sort the second array and keep the first as a copy
      call crank(wksp2, sg)

      wksp1 = wksp1 - wksp2
      d = dot_product(wksp1, wksp1)

      en   = real(n, sp)
      en3n = en**3 - en
      aved = en3n/6.0_sp - (sf + sg)/12.0_sp
      fac  = (1.0_sp - sf/en3n) * (1.0_sp - sg/en3n)
      vard = ((en-1.0_sp)*en**2*(en+1.0_sp)**2/36.0_sp) * fac
      zd   = (d - aved) / sqrt(vard)
      probd = erfcc(abs(zd) / sqrt(2.0_sp))
      rs   = (1.0_sp - (6.0_sp/en3n)*(d + (sf+sg)/12.0_sp)) / sqrt(fac)

      fac = (1.0_sp + rs)*(1.0_sp - rs)
      if (fac > 0.0_sp) then
         t  = rs * sqrt((en-2.0_sp)/fac)
         df = en - 2.0_sp
         probrs = betai(0.5_sp*df, 0.5_sp, df/(df + t**2))
      else
         probrs = 0.0_sp
      end if

      deallocate(wksp1, wksp2)
   end subroutine spear

end module nr_mod

   real(sp) :: d, zd, probd, rs, probrs

   data2 = [5.0_sp, 4.0_sp, 3.0_sp, 2.0_sp, 1.0_sp]

   print *, 'zd      =', zd
   print *, 'probd   =', probd
   print *, 'rs      =', rs

  subroutine gasdev_s(harvest)

      harvest = g
      gaus_stored = .false.

        call random_number(v1)
        call random_number(v2)

        v2 = 2.0_sp * v2 - 1.0_sp

program GasDevDemo
  implicit none

  ! Kind parameters
  integer, parameter :: i4b = selected_int_kind(9)   ! at least 32‑bit integer
  integer, parameter :: sp  = kind(1.0)              ! single precision real

  ! Demonstration variables
  real(sp) :: scalar_result
  real(sp), dimension(10) :: vector_result

  ! Call the scalar generator
  call gasdev_s(scalar_result)
  print *, 'Scalar Gaussian deviate:', scalar_result

  ! Call the vector generator
  call gasdev_v(vector_result)
  print *, 'Vector Gaussian deviates:'
  print *, vector_result

contains

  ! ------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Uniform random number generator for an array (vectorised version).
  ! ------------------------------------------------------------
  subroutine ran1_array(x)
    implicit none
    real(sp), intent(out) :: x(:)
    call random_number(x)
  end subroutine ran1_array

  ! ------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Scalar Gaussian random number generator (Box‑Muller)
  ! ------------------------------------------------------------
  subroutine gasdev_s(harvest)
    implicit none
    real(sp), intent(out) :: harvest
    real(sp) :: rsq, v1, v2
    real(sp), save :: g
    logical, save :: gaus_stored = .false.

    if (gaus_stored) then
      harvest = g
      gaus_stored = .false.
    else
      do
        call random_number(v1)
        call random_number(v2)
        v1 = 2.0_sp * v1 - 1.0_sp
        v2 = 2.0_sp * v2 - 1.0_sp
        rsq = v1**2 + v2**2
        if (rsq > 0.0_sp .and. rsq < 1.0_sp) exit
      end do
      rsq = sqrt(-2.0_sp * log(rsq) / rsq)
      harvest = v1 * rsq
      g = v2 * rsq
      gaus_stored = .true.
    end if
  end subroutine gasdev_s

  ! ------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Vector Gaussian random number generator (Box‑Muller, vectorised)
  ! ------------------------------------------------------------
  subroutine gasdev_v(harvest)
    implicit none
    real(sp), dimension(:), intent(out) :: harvest
    integer(i4b) :: n, ng, nn
    real(sp), dimension(size(harvest)) :: rsq, v1, v2
    logical, dimension(size(harvest)) :: mask
    real(sp), allocatable, save :: g(:)
    integer(i4b), save :: last_allocated = 0
    logical, save :: gaus_stored = .false.

    n = size(harvest)

    ! Allocate or re‑allocate the saved array "g" if the size changed
    if (n /= last_allocated) then
      if (allocated(g)) deallocate(g)
      allocate(g(n))
      last_allocated = n
      gaus_stored = .false.
    end if

    if (gaus_stored) then
      harvest = g
      gaus_stored = .false.
      return
    end if

    ng = 1
    do while (ng <= n)
      ! Generate uniform numbers for the remaining slots
      call ran1_array(v1(ng:n))
      call ran1_array(v2(ng:n))
      v1(ng:n) = 2.0_sp * v1(ng:n) - 1.0_sp
      v2(ng:n) = 2.0_sp * v2(ng:n) - 1.0_sp
      rsq(ng:n) = v1(ng:n)**2 + v2(ng:n)**2

      mask(ng:n) = (rsq(ng:n) > 0.0_sp .and. rsq(ng:n) < 1.0_sp)

      if (any(mask(ng:n))) then
        nn = count(mask(ng:n))
        v1(ng:ng+nn-1) = pack(v1(ng:n), mask(ng:n))
        v2(ng:ng+nn-1) = pack(v2(ng:n), mask(ng:n))
        rsq(ng:ng+nn-1) = pack(rsq(ng:n), mask(ng:n))
        ng = ng + nn
      else
        ! No acceptable points in this batch – generate another batch
        cycle
      end if
    end do

    rsq = sqrt(-2.0_sp * log(rsq) / rsq)
    harvest = v1 * rsq
    g = v2 * rsq
    gaus_stored = .true.
  end subroutine gasdev_v

end program GasDevDemo

  subroutine nrerror(message)
    character(*), intent(in) :: message
    print *, 'ERROR:', trim(message)
    stop 1
  end subroutine nrerror

  subroutine sncndn(uu, emmc, sn, cn, dn)
    implicit none
    real(kind=SP), intent(in) :: uu, emmc
    real(kind=SP), intent(out) :: sn, cn, dn
    real(kind=SP), parameter :: CA = 0.0003_sp
    integer, parameter :: MAXIT = 13
    integer :: i, ii, l
    real(kind=SP) :: a, b, c, d, emc, u
    real(kind=SP), dimension(MAXIT) :: em, en
    logical :: bo

    emc = emmc
    u = uu
    if (emc /= 0.0_sp) then
      bo = (emc < 0.0_sp)
      if (bo) then
        d = 1.0_sp - emc
        emc = -emc / d
        d = sqrt(d)
        u = d * u
      end if
      a = 1.0_sp
      dn = 1.0_sp
      do i = 1, MAXIT
        l = i
        em(i) = a
        emc = sqrt(emc)
        en(i) = emc
        c = 0.5_sp * (a + emc)
        if (abs(a - emc) <= CA * a) exit
        emc = a * emc
        a = c
      end do
      if (i > MAXIT) call nrerror('sncndn: convergence failed')
      u = c * u
      sn = sin(u)
      cn = cos(u)
      if (sn /= 0.0_sp) then
        a = cn / sn
        c = a * c
        do ii = l, 1, -1
          b = em(ii)
          a = c * a
          c = dn * c
          dn = (en(ii) + a) / (b + a)
          a = c / b
        end do
        a = 1.0_sp / sqrt(c**2 + 1.0_sp)
        sn = sign(a, sn)
        cn = c * sn
      end if
      if (bo) then
        a = dn
        dn = cn
        cn = a
        sn = sn / d
      end if
    else
      cn = 1.0_sp / cosh(u)
      dn = cn
      sn = tanh(u)
    end if
  end subroutine sncndn

end program sncndn_demo

         jhi = n + 1
      else

            do

               if (jhi > n) then

                  inc = inc + inc

  integer                    :: i
  real(sp)                   :: pi

  ! Initialise a simple test signal (two sinusoids)
  pi = acos(-1.0_sp)
  do i = 1, n

     y(i) = sin(5.0_sp*x(i)) + 0.2_sp*sin(20.0_sp*x(i))
  end do

  ofac = 2.0_sp   ! oversampling factor
  hifac = 3.0_sp  ! high‑frequency factor

  call period(x, y, ofac, hifac, px, py, jmax, prob)

  print *, ' jmax =', jmax
  print *, ' prob =', prob
  print *, ' First few periods (px) and powers (py):'
  do i = 1, min(10, size(px))
     print *, i, px(i), py(i)
  end do

    real(sp)                    :: ave, cwtau, effm, expy, pnow, sumc, sumcy, sums, sumsh, sumsy, swtau, var, wtau, xave, xdif, xmax, xmin

    if (init) then

       nullify(px, py)
    else
       if (associated(px)) deallocate(px)
       if (associated(py)) deallocate(py)
    end if

    nout = int(0.5_sp*ofac*hifac*real(n, sp), kind=i4b)
    allocate(px(nout), py(nout))
    deallocate(px)
    allocate(tmp1(n), tmp2(n), wi(n), wpi(n), wpr(n), wr(n))

    if (var == 0.0_sp) call nrerror('zero variance in period')

    xmin = minval(x)
    xdif = xmax - xmin
    xave = 0.5_sp*(xmax + xmin)
    pnow = 1.0_sp/(xdif*ofac)

    tmp1 = twopi_dp * ((x - xave)*pnow)
    wpr  = -2.0_dp*sin(0.5_dp*tmp1)**2
    wpi  = sin(tmp1)
    wr   = cos(tmp1)

       sumc  = dot_product(tmp2, tmp2)

       sumcy = dot_product(real(y - ave, dp), tmp2)

    ave  = sum1 / real(n, sp)
    sum2 = sum((v - ave)**2)

    real(sp), dimension(:), intent(in)  :: arr
    real(sp), dimension(:), intent(out) :: heap
    integer :: i, j, k, m, n

    m = size(heap)
    n = size(arr)
    if (m > n/2 .or. m < 1) then

       stop
    end if

    call sort(heap)

          j = 1

             if (k /= m) then

             call swap(heap(k), heap(j))

    end do

    implicit none

          j = j - 1

      ! Return the 1‑based index of the minimum element of a 1‑D array
      REAL(KIND=SP), INTENT(IN) :: arr(:)
      INTEGER :: idx, i
      REAL(KIND=SP) :: minval
      IF (SIZE(arr) == 0) THEN
         CALL nrerror ("iminloc: empty array")
      END IF
      minval = arr(1)
      idx    = 1
      DO i = 2, SIZE(arr)
         IF (arr(i) < minval) THEN
            minval = arr(i)
            idx    = i
         END IF
      END DO
   END FUNCTION iminloc

   SUBROUTINE nrerror (message)
      CHARACTER(*), INTENT(IN) :: message
      PRINT *, "NRERROR:", TRIM(message)
      STOP 1
   END SUBROUTINE nrerror

   !================================================================
   !  Polint – polynomial interpolation (Numerical Recipes)
   !================================================================
   SUBROUTINE polint (xa, ya, x, y, dy)
      IMPLICIT NONE

    stop 2
  end subroutine nrerror

    integer, parameter :: MAXIT = 100
    real(kind=SP), parameter :: EPS = epsilon(x)
    real(kind=SP), parameter :: FPMIN = tiny(x)/EPS
    integer :: k
    real(kind=SP) :: fact, prev, sm, term
    real(kind=SP), parameter :: EULER = 0.5772156649_sp

    call assert(x > 0.0_sp, 'ei arg'
    if (x < FPMIN) then
      ei_res = log(x) + EULER
    else if (x <= -log(EPS)) then
      sm = 0.0_sp
      fact = 1.0_sp
      do k = 1, MAXIT

        if (term < prev) then

        else

      end do
      if (k > MAXIT) call nrerror('asymptotic failed in ei')
      ei_res = exp(x) * (1.0_sp + sm) / x
    end if
  end function ei

program ftest_demo

  ! Kind parameters
  integer, parameter :: i4b = selected_int_kind(9)   ! at least 4‑byte integer
  integer, parameter :: sp  = kind(1.0)               ! single precision
  integer, parameter :: dp  = kind(1.0d0)             ! double precision

  ! Test data (hard‑coded)
  real(sp), dimension(:), allocatable :: data1, data2
  real(sp) :: f, prob

  ! Allocate and initialise small representative arrays
  allocate(data1(4))
  data1 = [1.0_sp, 2.0_sp, 3.0_sp, 4.0_sp]
  allocate(data2(5))
  data2 = [2.0_sp, 3.0_sp, 4.0_sp, 5.0_sp, 6.0_sp]

  call ftest(data1, data2, f, prob)
  print *, "F statistic =", f
  print *, "Two‑tailed probability =", prob

contains

  subroutine ftest(data1, data2, f, prob)
    implicit none
    real(sp), intent(in)  :: data1(:), data2(:)
    real(sp), intent(out) :: f, prob
    integer(i4b)          :: n1, n2
    real(sp)              :: ave1, ave2, df1, df2, var1, var2
    real(dp)              :: a, b, x, bet_res

    n1 = size(data1)
    n2 = size(data2)

    call avevar(data1, ave1, var1
    call avevar(data2, ave2, var2)

    if (var1 > var2) then
       f   = var1 / var2
       df1 = real(n1 - 1, sp)
       df2 = real(n2 - 1, sp)
    else
       f   = var2 / var1
       df1 = real(n2 - 1, sp)
       df2 = real(n1 - 1, sp)
    end if

    ! Compute the two‑tailed probability using the incomplete beta function
    a = 0.5_dp * real(df2, dp)
    b = 0.5_dp * real(df1, dp)
    x = real(df2, dp) / ( real(df2, dp) + real(df1, dp) * real(f, dp) )
    bet_res = betai(a, b, x)
    prob = 2.0_sp * real(bet_res, sp)
    if (prob > 1.0_sp) prob = 2.0_sp - prob
  end subroutine ftest

  subroutine avevar(x, ave, var)
    implicit none
    real(sp), intent(in)  :: x(:)
    real(sp), intent(out) :: ave, var
    integer(i4b)          :: n
    real(sp)              :: sumx, sumsq
    n = size(x)
    if (n == 0) then
       ave = 0.0_sp
       var = 0.0_sp
       return
    end if
    sumx = sum(x)
    ave  = sumx / real(n, sp)
    sumsq = sum( (x - ave)**2 )
    if (n > 1) then
       var = sumsq / real(n-1, sp)
    else
       var = 0.0_sp
    end if
  end subroutine avevar

  function betai(a, b, x) result(res)
    implicit none
    real(dp), intent(in) :: a, b, x
    real(dp)             :: res, bt, a1, b1, x1
    if (x < 0.0_dp .or. x > 1.0_dp) then
       res = 0.0_dp
       return
    end if
    if (x == 0.0_dp .or. x == 1.0_dp) then
       res = 0.0_dp
       return
    end if
    ! Compute the factor bt = exp(ln Gamma(a+b) - ln Gamma(a) - ln Gamma(b) + a*ln x + b*ln(1-x))
    bt = exp( lgamma(a+b) - lgamma(a) - lgamma(b) + a*log(x) + b*log(1.0_dp - x) )
    if (x < (a+1.0_dp)/(a+b+2.0_dp)) then
       res = bt * betacf(a, b, x) / a
    else
       res = 1.0_dp - bt * betacf(b, a, 1.0_dp - x) / b
    end if
  end function betai

  function betacf(a, b, x) result(cf)
    implicit none
    real(dp), intent(in) :: a, b, x
    real(dp)             :: cf
    integer, parameter   :: MAXIT = 100
    real(dp), parameter  :: EPS = 3.0e-7_dp
    real(dp), parameter  :: FPMIN = 1.0e-30_dp
    integer :: m, m2
    real(dp) :: aa, c, d, del, h, qab, qam, qap

    qab = a + b
    qap = a + 1.0_dp
    qam = a - 1.0_dp
    c = 1.0_dp
    d = 1.0_dp - qab * x / qap
    if (abs(d) < FPMIN) d = FPMIN
    d = 1.0_dp / d
    h = d
    do m = 1, MAXIT
       m2 = 2 * m
       ! Even step
       aa = real(m, dp) * (b - real(m, dp)) * x / ((qam + real(m2, dp)) * (a + real(m2, dp)))
       d = 1.0_dp + aa * d
       if (abs(d) < FPMIN) d = FPMIN
       c = 1.0_dp + aa / c
       if (abs(c) < FPMIN) c = FPMIN
       d = 1.0_dp / d
       h = h * d * c
       ! Odd step
       aa = -(a + real(m, dp)) * (qab + real(m, dp)) * x / ((a + real(m2, dp)) * (qap + real(m2, dp)))
       d = 1.0_dp + aa * d
       if (abs(d) < FPMIN) d = FPMIN
       c = 1.0_dp + aa / c
       if (abs(c) < FPMIN) c = FPMIN
       d = 1.0_dp / d
       del = d * c
       h = h * del
       if (abs(del - 1.0_dp) < EPS) exit
    end do
    cf = h
  end function betacf

end program ftest_demo

    integer(int32), intent(in) :: l, m
    real(real32), intent(in) :: x
    real(real32) :: res
    integer(int32) :: ll
    real(real32) :: pll, pmm, pmmp1, somx2

     call avevar(data, ave, var)
     write(*,'(1x,f6.2,2f12.2)') shift, ave, var
  end do
contains

  subroutine ran_seed(sequence)
    integer, intent(in) :: sequence
    integer, allocatable :: seed(:)
    integer :: n, i
    call random_seed(size=n)
    allocate(seed(n-1))
    do i = 1, n
       seed(i) = mod(sequence + i - 1, 2147483647)
    end do
    call random_seed(put=seed)
    deallocate(seed)
  end subroutine ran_seed

  subroutine gasdev(data)
    real(kind=sp), intent(out) :: data(:)
    integer :: n, i
    real(kind=sp) :: u1, u2, r, theta, pi
    n = size(data)
    pi = acos(-1.0_sp)
    i = 1
    do while (i <= n-1)
       call random_number(u1)
       call random_number(u2)
       if (u1 == 0.0_sp) cycle
       r = sqrt(-2.0_sp*log(u1))
       theta = 2.0_sp*pi*u2
       data(i)   = r*cos(theta)
       data(i+1) = r*sin(theta)
       i = i + 2
    end do
    if (i == n) then
       call random_number(u1)
       call random_number(u2)
       if (u1 == 0.0_sp) u1 = 1.0_sp
       r = sqrt(-2.0_sp*log(u1))
       theta = 2.0_sp*pi*u2

    end if

    end if
  end subroutine avevar

    INTEGER, PARAMETER :: max_iter = 20
    REAL(sp), PARAMETER :: tol = 1.0e-8_sp
    INTEGER :: iter
    REAL(sp) :: f, df, dv
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(3) :: y, fvec
    REAL(sp) :: x

    ! Initial guess is already in v(1) (set by the main program).
    DO iter = 1, max_iter
       !--- integrate from x1 to x2 using a simple RK4 scheme ---------
       x = x1
       CALL load(x1, v, y)          ! initialise y at the left boundary
       DO WHILE (x < x2)
          CALL rk4_step(x, y, dx, derivs, y)
          x = x + dx
       END DO

       !--- evaluate the boundary condition residual -----------------
       CALL score(x2, y, fvec)
       f = fvec(1)

       IF (ABS(f) < tol) THEN
          check = .FALSE.
          RETURN
       END IF

       !--- approximate derivative df/dv using a finite difference ---
       dv = 1.0e-6_sp * MAX(1.0_sp, ABS(v(1)))
       v(1) = v(1) + dv
       CALL load(x1, v, y)
       x = x1
       DO WHILE (x < x2)
          CALL rk4_step(x, y, dx, derivs, y)
          x = x + dx
       END DO
       CALL score(x2, y, fvec)
       df = (fvec(1) - f) / dv

       !--- Newton update --------------------------------------------
       IF (df == 0.0_sp) THEN
          check = .TRUE.
          RETURN
       END IF
       v(1) = v(1) - f/df
    END DO

    check = .TRUE.   ! did not converge within max_iter
  END SUBROUTINE newt

  !=================================================================
  ! Subroutine RK4_STEP – one Runge–Kutta 4th‑order step.
  !=================================================================
  SUBROUTINE rk4_step(x, y, h, derivs, yout)
    REAL(sp), INTENT(IN)    :: x, h
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(IN)  :: y
    INTERFACE
       SUBROUTINE derivs(x, y, dydx)
         USE iso_fortran_env, ONLY: real32
         REAL(real32), INTENT(IN)  :: x
         REAL(real32), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(IN)  :: y
         REAL(real32), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(OUT) :: dydx
       END SUBROUTINE derivs
    END INTERFACE
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(OUT) :: yout
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(SIZE(y)) :: k1, k2, k3, k4, yt

    CALL derivs(x, y, k1)
    yt = y + 0.5_sp*h*k1
    CALL derivs(x+0.5_sp*h, yt, k2)
    yt = y + 0.5_sp*h*k2
    CALL derivs(x+0.5_sp*h, yt, k3)
    yt = y + h*k3
    CALL derivs(x+h, yt, k4)
    yout = y + h/6.0_sp*(k1 + 2.0_sp*k2 + 2.0_sp*k3 + k4)
  END SUBROUTINE rk4_step

  !=================================================================
  ! Subroutine LOAD – prepares the state vector at the left boundary.
  !=================================================================
  SUBROUTINE load(x1, v, y)
    REAL(sp), INTENT(IN)  :: x1
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(IN)  :: v
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(OUT) :: y
    REAL(sp) :: y1
    y(3) = v(1)
    y1 = MERGE(gamma, -gamma, MOD(n-m,2) == 0)
    y(2) = -(y(3)-c2)*y1/(2.0_sp*(m+1_i4b))
    y(1) = y1 + y(2)*dx
  END SUBROUTINE load

  !=================================================================
  ! Subroutine SCORE – evaluates the shooting residual at x2.
  !=================================================================
  SUBROUTINE score(x2, y, f)
    REAL(sp), INTENT(IN)  :: x2
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(IN)  :: y
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(OUT) :: f
    f(1) = MERGE(y(2), y(1), MOD(n-m,2) == 0)
  END SUBROUTINE score

  !=================================================================
  ! Subroutine DERIVS – right‑hand side of the ODE system.
  !=================================================================
  SUBROUTINE derivs(x, y, dydx)
    REAL(sp), INTENT(IN)  :: x
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(IN)  :: y
    REAL(sp), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(OUT) :: dydx
    dydx(1) = y(2)
    dydx(2) = (2.0_sp*x*(m+1_i4b)*y(2) - (y(3)-c2*x*x)*y(1)) / (1.0_sp - x*x)
    dydx(3) = 0.0_sp
  END SUBROUTINE derivs

    real(real32), intent(in) :: a, b, x
    integer, parameter :: MAXIT = 100
    real(real32), parameter :: EPS = 3.0e-7_real32
    real(real32), parameter :: FPMIN = tiny(1.0_real32)
    integer :: m, m2
    real(real32) :: aa, c, d, del, h, qab, qap, qam

    qab = a + b
    qap = a + 1.0_real32
    qam = a - 1.0_real32
    c = 1.0_real32
    d = 1.0_real32 - qab*x/qap
    if (abs(d) < FPMIN) d = FPMIN
    d = 1.0_real32/d
    h = d
    do m = 1, MAXIT
       m2 = 2*m
       aa = m*(b - m)*x/((qam + m2)*(a + m2))
       d = 1.0_real32 + aa*d
       if (abs(d) < FPMIN) d = FPMIN
       c = 1.0_real32 + aa/c
       if (abs(c) < FPMIN) c = FPMIN
       d = 1.0_real32/d
       h = h*d*c
       aa = -(a + m)*(qab + m)*x/((a + m2)*(qap + m2))
       d = 1.0_real32 + aa*d
       if (abs(d) < FPMIN) d = FPMIN
       c = 1.0_real32 + aa/c
       if (abs(c) < FPMIN) c = FPMIN
       d = 1.0_real32/d
       del = d*c
       h = h*del
       if (abs(del - 1.0_real32) < EPS) exit
    end do
    betacf = h
  end function betacf

program fourrow_3d_demo
   implicit none
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Kind parameters (as required by the transformation rules)
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   integer, parameter :: sp = kind(1.0)          ! single precision real
   integer, parameter :: dp = kind(1.0d0)        ! double precision real
   integer, parameter :: i4b = selected_int_kind(9)   ! at least 32‑bit integer

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Constants
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   real(dp), parameter :: pi_d = acos(-1.0_dp)

   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   ! Test data – a small 2×2×4 complex array (power‑of‑2 in the 3rd dim)
   !-------------------------------------------------------------------
   integer(i4b), parameter :: nx = 2, ny = 2, nz = 4
   complex(sp), dimension(nx,ny,nz) :: data
   integer(i4b) :: i, j, k

   ! Initialise the array with a simple pattern
   do k = 1, nz
      do j = 1, ny
         do i = 1, nx
            data(i,j,k) = cmplx( real(i+j+k, sp), real(i*j*k, sp), kind=sp )
         end do
      end do
   end do

   print *, '--- Input data (slice k=1) ---'
   do j = 1, ny
      print '(4("(",f6.2,",",f6.2,") "))', (data(i,j,1), i=1,nx)
   end do

   call fourrow_3d(data, isign = 1)

   print *, '--- Output data after fourrow_3d (slice k=1) ---'
   do j = 1, ny
      print '(4("(",f6.2,",",f6.2,") "))', (data(i,j,1), i=1,nx)
   end do

contains

   !=================================================================
   !  Subroutine: fourrow_3d
   !  3‑D radix‑2 FFT applied along the third dimension.
   !=================================================================
   subroutine fourrow_3d(data, isign)
      implicit none
      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! Arguments
      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      complex(sp), dimension(:,:,:), intent(inout) :: data
      integer(i4b),               intent(in)    :: isign
      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      ! Locals
      !----------------------------------------------------------------
      integer(i4b) :: n, i, istep, j, m, mmax, n2
      real(dp)    :: theta
      complex(sp), dimension(size(data,1),size(data,2)) :: temp
      complex(dp) :: w, wp
      complex(sp) :: ws

      n = size(data,3)
      call assert( iand(n, n-1) == 0, 'n must be a power of 2 in fourrow_3d' )
      n2 = n / 2
      j  = n2

      ! Bit‑reversal permutation on the third index
      do i = 1, n-2
         if (j > i) call swap(data(:,:,j+1), data(:,:,i+1))
         m = n2
         do
            if (m < 2 .or. j < m) exit
            j = j - m
            m = m / 2
         end do
         j = j + m
      end do

      ! Danielson‑Lanczos section
      mmax = 1
      do
         if (n <= mmax) exit
         istep = 2 * mmax
         theta = pi_d / ( real(isign,dp) * real(mmax,dp) )
         wp = cmplx( -2.0_dp * sin(0.5_dp*theta)**2, sin(theta), kind=dp )
         w  = cmplx( 1.0_dp, 0.0_dp, kind=dp )

         do m = 1, mmax
            ws = w   ! conversion from double to single precision complex
            do i = m, n, istep
               j = i + mmax
               temp = ws * data(:,:,j)
               data(:,:,j) = data(:,:,i) - temp
               data(:,:,i) = data(:,:,i) + temp
            end do
            w = w*wp + w
         end do
         mmax = istep
      end do

   end subroutine fourrow_3d

   !=================================================================
   !  Subroutine: assert
   !  Simple runtime check – aborts program if condition is false.
   !=================================================================
   subroutine assert(cond, msg)
      implicit none
      logical, intent(in)          :: cond
      character(*), intent(in)     :: msg
      if (.not. cond) then
         print *, 'ASSERTION FAILED: ', trim(msg)
         stop 1
      end if
   end subroutine assert

   !=================================================================
   !  Subroutine: swap
   !  Exchanges the contents of two same‑shaped 2‑D complex arrays.
   !=================================================================
   subroutine swap(a, b)
      implicit none
      complex(sp), dimension(:,:), intent(inout) :: a, b
      complex(sp), allocatable :: tmp(:,:)
      integer :: sz1, sz2
      sz1 = size(a,1)
      sz2 = size(a,2)
      allocate(tmp(sz1,sz2))
      tmp = a
      a   = b
      b   = tmp
      deallocate(tmp)
      tmp(1,1) = cmplx(0.0_sp,0.0_sp,kind=sp)
   end subroutine swap

end program fourrow_3d_demo

! Stand‑alone Fortran 90 program implementing the Numerical Recipes
! subroutine QRSOLV together with minimal replacements for the external
! utilities ASSERT_EQ and RSOLV.  The program uses a small hard‑coded
! example (n=3) and prints the resulting vector B after solving the

PROGRAM qrsolv_demo
  IMPLICIT NONE

  ! Kind parameters (allowed only ISO_FORTRAN_ENV and ISO_C_BINDING)
  INTEGER, PARAMETER :: SP = KIND(1.0)          ! single precision kind
  INTEGER, PARAMETER :: I4B = SELECTED_INT_KIND(9)  ! at least 4‑byte integer

  INTEGER(I4B) :: n
  REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:,:), ALLOCATABLE :: a
  REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:),   ALLOCATABLE :: c, d, b

  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Hard‑coded test data (n = 3).  These numbers are chosen only to
  ! illustrate the algorithm; they are not derived from a real QR
  ! decomposition.
  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  n = 3
  ALLOCATE(a(n,n), c(n), d(n), b(n))

  a = RESHAPE([ &
       1.0_SP, 0.5_SP, -0.2_SP, &
       0.0_SP, 2.0_SP,  0.3_SP, &
       0.0_SP, 0.0_SP,  3.0_SP ], SHAPE(a))

  c = [ 1.0_SP, 2.0_SP, 3.0_SP ]   ! diagonal elements of R (as used in QR)
  d = [ 1.0_SP, 2.0_SP, 3.0_SP ]   ! also diagonal – RSOLV expects the same
  b = [ 4.0_SP, 5.0_SP, 6.0_SP ]   ! right‑hand side vector (will be modified)

  CALL qrsolv(a, c, d, b)

  WRITE *, 'Resulting vector B after QRSOLV:'
  PRINT *, b

CONTAINS

  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Subroutine QRSOLV – solves A·x = b using a QR‑decomposed matrix.
  ! The implementation follows the original Numerical Recipes code.
  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  SUBROUTINE qrsolv(a, c, d, b)
    IMPLICIT NONE
    REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:,:), INTENT(IN)    :: a
    REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:),   INTENT(IN)    :: c, d
    REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:),   INTENT(INOUT) :: b
    INTEGER(I4B) :: j, n_local
    REAL(SP)    :: tau

    n_local = assert_eq([SIZE(a,1), SIZE(a,2), SIZE(b), SIZE(c), SIZE(d)], 'qrsolv')
    DO j = 1, n_local-1
       tau = DOT_PRODUCT(a(j:n_local, j), b(j:n_local)) / c(j)
       b(j:n_local) = b(j:n_local) - tau * a(j:n_local, j)
    END DO
    CALL rsolv(a, d, b)
  END SUBROUTINE qrsolv

  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Subroutine RSOLV – back substitution for an upper‑triangular matrix.
  ! The upper triangle of A (including the diagonal) stores the matrix R.
  ! The diagonal elements are also supplied in D for safety (as in the
  ! original NR routine).
  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  SUBROUTINE rsolv(a, d, b)
    IMPLICIT NONE
    REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:,:), INTENT(IN)    :: a
    REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:),   INTENT(IN)    :: d
    REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:),   INTENT(INOUT) :: b
    INTEGER(I4B) :: i, j, n_local

    n_local = SIZE(a,1)
    DO i = n_local, 1, -1
       b(i) = b(i) / d(i)
       DO j = 1, i-1
          b(j) = b(j) - a(j,i) * b(i)

  INTEGER(I4B) FUNCTION assert_eq(sizes, routine_name)

    CHARACTER(*),               INTENT(IN) :: routine_name

!====================================================================
! Stand‑alone Fortran 90 program implementing the Numerical Recipes
! subroutine QRSOLV together with minimal replacements for the external
! utilities ASSERT_EQ and RSOLV.  The program uses a small hard‑coded
! example (n=3) and prints the resulting vector B after solving the
! linear system.
!====================================================================
PROGRAM qrsolv_demo
  IMPLICIT NONE

  ! Kind parameters (allowed only ISO_FORTRAN_ENV and ISO_C_BINDING)
  INTEGER, PARAMETER :: SP = KIND(1.0)          ! single precision kind
  INTEGER, PARAMETER :: I4B = SELECTED_INT_KIND(9)  ! at least 4‑byte integer

  INTEGER(I4B) :: n
  REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:,:), ALLOCATABLE :: a
  REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:),   ALLOCATABLE :: c, d, b

  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Hard‑coded test data (n = 3).  These numbers are chosen only to
  ! illustrate the algorithm; they are not derived from a real QR
  ! decomposition.
  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  n = 3
  ALLOCATE(a(n,n), c(n), d(n), b(n))

  a = RESHAPE([ &
       1.0_SP, 0.5_SP, -0.2_SP, &
       0.0_SP, 2.0_SP,  0.3_SP, &
       0.0_SP, 0.0_SP,  3.0_SP ], SHAPE(a))

  c = [ 1.0_SP, 2.0_SP, 3.0_SP ]   ! diagonal elements of R (as used in QR)
  d = [ 1.0_SP, 2.0_SP, 3.0_SP ]   ! also diagonal – RSOLV expects the same
  b = [ 4.0_SP, 5.0_SP, 6.0_SP ]   ! right‑hand side vector (will be modified)

  CALL qrsolv(a, c, d, b)

  PRINT *, 'Resulting vector B after QRSOLV:'
  PRINT *, b

CONTAINS

  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Subroutine QRSOLV – solves A·x = b using a QR‑decomposed matrix.
  ! The implementation follows the original Numerical Recipes code.
  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  SUBROUTINE qrsolv(a, c, d, b)
    IMPLICIT NONE
    REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:,:), INTENT(IN)    :: a
    REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:),   INTENT(IN)    :: c, d
    REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:),   INTENT(INOUT) :: b
    INTEGER(I4B) :: j, n_local
    REAL(SP)    :: tau

    n_local = assert_eq([SIZE(a,1), SIZE(a,2), SIZE(b), SIZE(c), SIZE(d)], 'qrsolv')
    DO j = 1, n_local-1
       tau = DOT_PRODUCT(a(j:n_local, j), b(j:n_local)) / c(j)
       b(j:n_local) = b(j:n_local) - tau * a(j:n_local, j)
    END DO
    CALL rsolv(a, d, b)
  END SUBROUTINE qrsolv

  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Subroutine RSOLV – back substitution for an upper‑triangular matrix.
  ! The upper triangle of A (including the diagonal) stores the matrix R.
  ! The diagonal elements are also supplied in D for safety (as in the
  ! original NR routine).
  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  SUBROUTINE rsolv(a, d, b)
    IMPLICIT NONE
    REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:,:), INTENT(IN)    :: a
    REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:),   INTENT(IN)    :: d
    REAL(SP), DIMENSION(:),   INTENT(INOUT) :: b
    INTEGER(I4B) :: i, j, n_local

    n_local = SIZE(a,1)
    DO i = n_local, 1, -1
       b(i) = b(i) / d(i)
       DO j = 1, i-1
          b(j) = b(j) - a(j,i) * b(i)
       END DO
    END DO
  END SUBROUTINE rsolv

  !------------------------------------------------------------------
  INTEGER(I4B) FUNCTION assert_eq(sizes, routine_name)
    IMPLICIT NONE
    INTEGER(I4B), DIMENSION(:), INTENT(IN) :: sizes
    CHARACTER(*),               INTENT(IN) :: routine_name

          STOP 1

    END DO

  END FUNCTION assert_eq

!  routine (as described in Numerical Recipes).  The program computes the

PROGRAM xlaguer
  USE, INTRINSIC :: iso_fortran_env, ONLY: int32, real32
  IMPLICIT NONE

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Kind parameters (matching the original code's naming conventions)
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  INTEGER, PARAMETER :: i4b = int32
  INTEGER, PARAMETER :: sp  = real32               ! single precision
  INTEGER, PARAMETER :: csp = KIND((0.0_sp,0.0_sp)) ! complex single

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Problem‑specific parameters
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  INTEGER(i4b), PARAMETER :: M = 4, MP1 = M+1, NTRY = 21
  REAL(sp),    PARAMETER :: EPS = 1.0e-6_sp

  COMPLEX(csp) :: x
  COMPLEX(csp), DIMENSION(MP1) :: a
  COMPLEX(csp), DIMENSION(NTRY) :: y

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Initialise the polynomial coefficients (a(1) is the constant term)
  !   a(1) = 0 + 2 i
  !   a(2) = 0 + 0 i
  !   a(3) = -1 - 2 i
  !   a(4) = 0 + 0 i
  !   a(5) = 1 + 0 i   ->  x^4 term
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  DATA a / (0.0_sp,2.0_sp), (0.0_sp,0.0_sp), (-1.0_sp,-2.0_sp), &
            (0.0_sp,0.0_sp), (1.0_sp,0.0_sp) /

  WRITE(*,'(/1x,t16,a4,t29,a7,t39,a5/)') 'Real','Complex','#iter'

  n = 0
  DO i = 1, NTRY
     x = CMPLX( (REAL(i,sp)-11.0_sp)/10.0_sp, &
                (REAL(i,sp)-11.0_sp)/10.0_sp, KIND=csp )
     CALL laguer(a, x, its)

     IF (n == 0) 
        n = 1
        y(1) = x
        WRITE(*,'(1x,i5,2f15.6,i5)') n, REAL(x,sp), AIMAG(x), its
     ELSE
        IF (ANY( ABS(x - y(1:n)) <= EPS*ABS(x) )) CYCLE
        n = n + 1
        y(n) = x
        WRITE(*,'(1x,i5,2f15.6,i5)') n, REAL(x,sp), AIMAG(x), its
     END IF
  END DO

CONTAINS

  !===================================================================
  !  Laguerre's method for a complex polynomial.
  !  Input:
  !     a  – complex coefficients a(1) .. a(MP1)   (a(1) = constant term)
  !     x  – initial guess (on entry) and refined root (on exit)
  !  Output:
  !     its – number of iterations performed (max 30)
  !===================================================================
  SUBROUTINE laguer(a, x, its)
    COMPLEX(csp), INTENT(IN)  :: a(:)
    COMPLEX(csp), INTENT(INOUT) :: x
    INTEGER(i4b), INTENT(OUT) :: its

    INTEGER(i4b) :: maxit, n, i
    COMPLEX(csp) :: p, dp, d2p, g, h, sq, gp, gm, denom, dx
    REAL(sp) :: eps_local

    maxit    = 30
    eps_local = EPS
    n = SIZE(a) - 1   ! degree of the polynomial

    DO its = 1, maxit
       !--- Horner evaluation of polynomial and its derivatives ---
       p  = a(n+1)
       dp = (0.0_sp,0.0_sp)
       d2p = (0.0_sp,0.0_sp)
       DO i = n, 1, -1
          d2p = d2p*x + 2.0_sp*dp
          dp  = dp*x + p
          p   = p*x + a(i)
       END DO

       IF (ABS(p) < eps_local) EXIT   ! convergence

       g = dp / p
       h = g*g - d2p / p
       sq = SQRT( REAL(n-1,sp) * ( REAL(n,sp)*h - g*g ) )

       gp = g + sq
       gm = g - sq
       IF (ABS(gp) > ABS(gm)) THEN
          denom = gp
       ELSE
          denom = gm
       END IF

       IF (ABS(denom) == 0.0_sp) THEN
          dx = (0.0_sp,0.0_sp)
       ELSE
          dx = CMPLX( REAL(n,sp), 0.0_sp, KIND=csp) / denom
       END IF

       x = x - dx

       IF (ABS(dx) < eps_local) EXIT
    END DO

  END SUBROUTINE laguer

END PROGRAM xlaguer

    integer(i4b), intent(in) :: n
    real(sp), dimension(n) :: arr

    real(sp), intent(in)  :: x(:), y(:)
    real(sp), intent(in)  :: yp1, ypn
    real(sp), intent(out) :: y2(:)
    integer :: n, i, k
    real(sp), allocatable :: u(:)
    real(sp) :: sig, p, qn, un

    n = size(x)
    allocate(u(n-1))

    if (yp1 > 0.99e30_sp) then
       y2(1) = 0.0_sp
       u(1) = 0.0_sp
    else
       y2(1) = -0.5_sp
       u(1) = (3.0_sp/(x(2)-x(1))) * ((y(2)-y(1))/(x(2)-x(1)) - yp1)
    end if

       sig = (x(i)-x(i-1)) / (x(i+1)-x(i-1))
       p   = sig*y2(i-1) + 2.0_sp
       y2(i) = (sig-1.0_sp) / p
       u(i) = ( (y(i+1)-y(i))/(x(i+1)-x(i)) - (y(i)-y(i-1))/(x(i)-x(i-1)) )

       un = 0.0_sp

       qn = 0.5_sp
       un = (3.0_sp/(x(n)-x(n-1))) * (ypn - (y(n)-y(n-1))/(x(n)-x(n-1)))
    end if

    y2(n) = (un - qn*u(n-1)) / (qn*y2(n-1) + 1.0_sp)

    do k = n-1, 1, -1
       y2(k) = y2(k)*y2(k+1) + u(k)
    end do

    deallocate(u)
  end subroutine spline

    real(sp), intent(in) :: xa(:), ya(:), y2a(:), x

    real(sp) :: h, a, b

    klo = 1
    khi = n
    do while (khi - klo > 1)

    b = (x - xa(klo)) / h
    y = a*ya(klo) + b*ya(khi) + ((a**3 - a)*y2a(klo) + (b**3 - b)*y2a(khi)) * (h**2) / 6.0_sp
  end function splint

  subroutine cntab2(tab, h, hx, hy, hygx, hxgy, uygx, uxgy, uxy)
    !-----------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Compute entropies and dependency measures for a contingency table.
    ! The implementation follows the definitions used in Numerical Recipes.
    ! All logarithms are natural (base e).
    !-----------------------------------------------------------------
    integer(i4b), intent(in)  :: tab(:,:)
    real(sp),    intent(out) :: h, hx, hy, hygx, hxgy, uygx, uxgy, uxy

    integer(i4b) :: nr, nc, i, j
    real(sp) :: total, pij, pi, pj, logpij, logpi, logpj
    real(sp), allocatable :: p(:,:), pi_vec(:), pj_vec(:)

    nr = size(tab,1)
    nc = size(tab,2)
    total = real(sum(tab),sp)
    if (total <= 0.0_sp) then
       h = 0.0_sp; hx = 0.0_sp; hy = 0.0_sp
       hygx = 0.0_sp; hxgy = 0.0_sp
       uygx = 0.0_sp; uxgy = 0.0_sp; uxy = 0.0_sp
       return
    end if

    allocate(p(nr,nc))
    allocate(pi_vec(nr))
    allocate(pj_vec(nc))

    ! Joint probabilities
    p = real(tab,sp) / total

    ! Marginals
    pi_vec = sum(p, dim=2)   ! sum over columns -> size nr
    pj_vec = sum(p, dim=1)   ! sum over rows    -> size nc

    ! --- Entropy of the joint distribution H(X,Y)
    h = 0.0_sp
    do i = 1, nr
       do j = 1, nc
          pij = p(i,j)
          if (pij > 0.0_sp) h = h - pij*log(pij)
       end do
    end do

    ! --- Entropy of X marginal
    hx = 0.0_sp
    do i = 1, nr
       pi = pi_vec(i)
       if (pi > 0.0_sp) hx = hx - pi*log(pi)
    end do

    ! --- Entropy of Y marginal
    hy = 0.0_sp
    do j = 1, nc
       pj = pj_vec(j)
       if (pj > 0.0_sp) hy = hy - pj*log(pj)
    end do

    ! --- Conditional entropy H(Y|X)
    hygx = 0.0_sp
    do i = 1, nr
       pi = pi_vec(i)
       if (pi > 0.0_sp) then
          do j = 1, nc
             pij = p(i,j)
             if (pij > 0.0_sp) hygx = hygx - pij*log(pij/pi)
          end do
       end if
    end do

    ! --- Conditional entropy H(X|Y)
    hxgy = 0.0_sp
    do j = 1, nc
       pj = pj_vec(j)
       if (pj > 0.0_sp) then
          do i = 1, nr
             pij = p(i,j)
             if (pij > 0.0_sp) hxgy = hxgy - pij*log(pij/pj)
          end do
       end if
    end do

    ! --- Mutual information I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y)
    uygx = hx + hy - h   ! dependency of y on x (same as mutual information)
    uxgy = uygx           ! dependency of x on y – identical value
    uxy  = uygx           ! symmetrical dependency – same quantity

    deallocate(p, pi_vec, pj_vec)
  end subroutine cntab2

end program xcntab2

    END DO

program legendre_points_demo
  implicit none

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Demonstration of Gauss‑Lobatto Legendre points and weights.
  ! The core routines are taken from the original module and adapted
  ! to a self‑contained executable.
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------

  integer, parameter :: dp = kind(1.0d0)
  integer, parameter :: N = 4               ! polynomial order (example)
  real(dp), allocatable :: nodes(:), weight(:)

  integer :: i

  allocate(nodes(0:N))
  allocate(weight(0:N))

  ! Initialise the end‑points of the physical interval we want to map to.
  nodes(0) = -2.0_dp   ! left boundary (x0)
  nodes(N) =  2.0_dp   ! right boundary (xf)
  ! interior entries are not needed – they will be overwritten.

  call Legendre_Grid_Initialization('forward', nodes, weight)

  print *, 'Gauss‑Lobatto Legendre points (mapped to [-2,2]):'(1:100)
  do i = 0, N
     print '(I2,2X,F15.10)', i, nodes(i)
  end do

  print *, '\nCorresponding quadrature weights:'
  do i = 0, N
     print '(I2,2X,F15.10)', i, weight(i)
  end do

contains

  !===================================================================
  ! Computes the N+1 Gauss‑Lobatto Legendre points (x) and their
  ! quadrature weights (alpha) on the reference interval [-1,1].
  !===================================================================
  subroutine Legendre_Gauss_Lobatto_points(N, x, alpha)
    integer, intent(in)            :: N
    real(dp), intent(out)          :: x(0:N), alpha(0:N)

    real(dp), allocatable :: dx(:), L(:,:)
    real(dp) :: PI, eps
    integer :: k, M, iter, max_iter

    PI = 4.0_dp * atan(1.0_dp)
    eps = 1.0d-15
    max_iter = 1000

    M = N
    allocate(dx(0:M))
    allocate(L(0:N+1,0:M))

    ! Initial guess: Chebyshev‑Lobatto nodes (scaled to [-1,1])
    do k = 0, M
       x(k) = -cos(PI*real(k,dp)/real(N,dp))
    end do

    dx = 1.0_dp
    iter = 0
    do while (norm2(dx) > eps .and. iter < max_iter)
       iter = iter + 1

       L(0,:) = 1.0_dp
       L(1,:) = x

       ! Three‑term recurrence for Legendre polynomials
       do k = 1, N
          L(k+1,:) = ((2.0_dp*k+1.0_dp)/(k+1.0_dp)) * x * L(k,:) &
                     - (real(k,dp)/(k+1.0_dp)) * L(k-1,:)
       end do

       ! Newton iteration to enforce the Lobatto condition
       dx = ( L(N+1,:) - L(N-1,:) ) / ( (2.0_dp*N+1.0_dp) * L(N,:) )
       x  = x - dx
    end do

    if (iter >= max_iter) then
       print *, 'WARNING: Newton iteration did not converge within the limit.'
    end if

    alpha = 2.0_dp / ( real(N,dp)*(N+1) * L(N,:)**2 )

    deallocate(dx)
    deallocate(L)
  end subroutine Legendre_Gauss_Lobatto_points

  !===================================================================
  ! Initializes a Legendre‑Gauss‑Lobatto grid on an arbitrary interval.
  ! The input array `nodes` must have the correct size; its first and
  ! last elements define the physical interval to be mapped onto [-1,1].
  !===================================================================
  subroutine Legendre_Grid_Initialization(direction, nodes, alpha)
    character(len=*), intent(in)   :: direction
    real(dp), intent(inout)        :: nodes(0:)
    real(dp), intent(out)          :: alpha(0:)

    integer :: N
    real(dp) :: x0, xf

    N  = size(nodes) - 1
    x0 = nodes(0)
    xf = nodes(N)

    call Legendre_Gauss_Lobatto_points(N, nodes, alpha)

    ! Map from reference interval [-1,1] to [x0,xf]
    nodes = (x0 + xf)/2.0_dp + (xf - x0)/2.0_dp * nodes
  end subroutine Legendre_Grid_Initialization

  !===================================================================
  ! Euclidean norm of a real vector (L2 norm).
  !===================================================================
  real(dp) function norm2(v)

program legendre_points_demo
  implicit none

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Demonstration of Gauss‑Lobatto Legendre points and weights.
  ! The core routines are taken from the original module and adapted
  ! to a self‑contained executable.
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------

  integer, parameter :: dp = kind(1.0d0)
  integer, parameter :: N = 4               ! polynomial order (example)
  real(dp), allocatable :: nodes(:), weight(:)

  integer :: i

  allocate(nodes(0:N))
  allocate(weight(0:N))

  ! Initialise the end‑points of the physical interval we want to map to.
  nodes(0) = -2.0_dp   ! left boundary (x0)
  nodes(N) =  2.0_dp   ! right boundary (xf)
  ! interior entries are not needed – they will be overwritten.

  call Legendre_Grid_Initialization('forward', nodes, weight)

  print *, 'Gauss‑Lobatto Legendre points (mapped to [-2,2]):'
  do i = 0, N
     print '(I2,2X,F15.10)', i, nodes(i)
  end do

  print *, '\nCorresponding quadrature weights:'
  do i = 0, N
     print '(I2,2X,F15.10)', i, weight(i)
  end do

contains

  !===================================================================
  ! Computes the N+1 Gauss‑Lobatto Legendre points (x) and their
  ! quadrature weights (alpha) on the reference interval [-1,1].
  !===================================================================
  subroutine Legendre_Gauss_Lobatto_points(N, x, alpha)
    integer, intent(in)            :: N
    real(dp), intent(out)          :: x(0:N), alpha(0:N)

    real(dp), allocatable :: dx(:), L(:,:)
    real(dp) :: PI, eps
    integer :: k, M, iter, max_iter

    PI = 4.0_dp * atan(1.0_dp)
    eps = 1.0d-15
    max_iter = 1000

    M = N
    allocate(dx(0:M))
    allocate(L(0:N+1,0:M))

    ! Initial guess: Chebyshev‑Lobatto nodes (scaled to [-1,1])
    do k = 0, M
       x(k) = -cos(PI*real(k,dp)/real(N,dp))
    end do

    dx = 1.0_dp
    iter = 0
    do while (norm2(dx) > eps .and. iter < max_iter)
       iter = iter + 1

       L(0,:) = 1.0_dp
       L(1,:) = x

       ! Three‑term recurrence for Legendre polynomials
       do k = 1, N
          L(k+1,:) = ((2.0_dp*k+1.0_dp)/(k+1.0_dp)) * x * L(k,:) &
                     - (real(k,dp)/(k+1.0_dp)) * L(k-1,:)
       end do

       ! Newton iteration to enforce the Lobatto condition
       dx = ( L(N+1,:) - L(N-1,:) ) / ( (2.0_dp*N+1.0_dp) * L(N,:) )
       x  = x - dx
    end do

    if (iter >= max_iter) then
       print *, 'WARNING: Newton iteration did not converge within the limit.'
    end if

    alpha = 2.0_dp / ( real(N,dp)*(N+1) * L(N,:)**2 )

    deallocate(dx)
    deallocate(L)
  end subroutine Legendre_Gauss_Lobatto_points

  !===================================================================
  ! Initializes a Legendre‑Gauss‑Lobatto grid on an arbitrary interval.
  ! The input array `nodes` must have the correct size; its first and
  ! last elements define the physical interval to be mapped onto [-1,1].
  !===================================================================
  subroutine Legendre_Grid_Initialization(direction, nodes, alpha)
    character(len=*), intent(in)   :: direction
    real(dp), intent(inout)        :: nodes(0:)
    real(dp), intent(out)          :: alpha(0:)

    integer :: N
    real(dp) :: x0, xf

    N  = size(nodes) - 1
    x0 = nodes(0)
    xf = nodes(N)

    call Legendre_Gauss_Lobatto_points(N, nodes, alpha)

    ! Map from reference interval [-1,1] to [x0,xf]
    nodes = (x0 + xf)/2.0_dp + (xf - x0)/2.0_dp * nodes
  end subroutine Legendre_Grid_Initialization

  !===================================================================
  ! Euclidean norm of a real vector (L2 norm).
  !===================================================================
  real(dp) function norm2(v)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: v(:)
    norm2 = sqrt(sum(v*v))
  end function norm2

end program legendre_points_demo

  ! and the analytic log forms that serve as checks

  q3 = hypgeo(a, b, c, -z*z)
  zi = cmplx(-y, x, kind=SPC)   ! i*z rotated by 90°
  q4 = 0.5_sp * log((1.0_sp + zi) / (1.0_sp - zi)) / zi

  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  ! Output the results – identical to the original format
  !-------------------------------------------------------------------
  print *, '2F1(0.5,1.0,1.5;Z**2) =', q1
  print *, 'check using log form   =', q2
  print *, '2F1(0.5,1.0,1.5;-Z**2)=', q3
  print *, 'check using log form   =', q4

contains
  !===================================================================
  !  Function: hypgeo
  !  Computes the Gauss hypergeometric function 2F1(a,b;c;z) by direct
  !  series summation:
  !        _2F1(a,b;c;z) = Σ_{n=0}^{∞} (a)_n (b)_n / (c)_n * z^n / n!
  !  The Pochhammer symbols (a)_n are generated recursively, which is
  !  numerically stable for the modest precision used here.
  !
  !  Convergence is monitored by the magnitude of the latest term.  The
  !  routine stops when |term| < eps*|sum| or when a hard iteration limit
  !  is reached.  For |z| close to 1 the series converges slowly, but this
  !  implementation is adequate for the demonstration values employed in
  !  the driver program.
  !===================================================================
  function hypgeo(a, b, c, z) result(res)
    complex(SPC), intent(in) :: a, b, c, z
    complex(SPC)             :: res, term
    integer                  :: n
    real(SP)                 :: eps
    integer, parameter :: max_iter = 10000

    eps = 1.0e-6_sp   ! tolerance appropriate for single precision

    res  = (0.0_sp, 0.0_sp)
    term = (1.0_sp, 0.0_sp)   ! n = 0 term
    res  = term

    do n = 1, max_iter
      term = term * (a + real(n-1, SP)) * (b + real(n-1, SP)) &
               / ((c + real(n-1, SP)) * real(n, SP)) * z
      res = res + term
      if (abs(term) < eps*abs(res)) exit
    end do

    if (n >= max_iter) then
      print *, 'WARNING: hypgeo series did not converge within', max_iter, 'iterations'
    end if
  end function hypgeo

end subroutine xhypgeo

  ! Parameters (same values as the original program)
  !--------------------------------------------------------------------
  integer, parameter :: N = 20

    call random_seed(size=n)
    allocate(seed(n-1))

  subroutine mnbrak(ax, bx, cx, fa, fb, fc, f)
    ! Bracket a minimum of a unimodal function (NR implementation)
    real(sp), intent(inout) :: ax, bx, cx, fa, fb, fc
    interface
       function f(x) result(val)
         import :: sp
         real(sp), intent(in) :: x
         real(sp) :: val
       end function f
    end interface
    real(sp) :: ulim, u, r, q, fu
    real(sp), parameter :: GLIMIT = 100.0_sp, TINY = 1.0e-20_sp

    fa = f(ax)
    fb = f(bx)
    if (fb > fa) then
       call swap(ax, bx)
       call swap(fa, fb)
    end if
    cx = bx + GOLD*(bx-ax)
    fc = f(cx)

    do while (.true.)
       if (fb <= fc) exit
       r = (bx-ax)*(fb-fc)
       q = (bx-cx)*(fb-fa)
       u = bx - ((bx-cx)*q - (bx-ax)*r) / &
           (2.0_sp*sign(max(abs(q-r),TINY), q-r))
       ulim = bx + GLIMIT*(cx-bx)

       if ((bx-u)*(u-cx) > 0.0_sp) then
          fu = f(u)
          if (fu < fc) then
             ax = bx
             bx = u
             fa = fb
             fb = fu
             exit
          else if (fu > fb) then
             cx = u
             fc = fu
             exit
          end if
          u = cx + GOLD*(cx-bx)
          fu = f(u)
       else if ((cx-u)*(u-ulim) > 0.0_sp) then
          fu = f(u)
          if (fu < fc) then
             bx = cx
             cx = u
             fb = fc
             fc = fu
             u = cx + GOLD*(cx-bx)
             fu = f(u)
          end if
       else if ((u-ulim)*(ulim-cx) >= 0.0_sp) then
          u = ulim
          fu = f(u)
       else
          u = cx + GOLD*(cx-bx)
          fu = f(u)
       end if

       ax = bx
       bx = cx
       cx = u
       fa = fb
       fb = fc
       fc = fu
    end do
  end subroutine mnbrak

    ! Golden‑section search for a minimum (NR implementation)
    real(sp), intent(in)  :: ax, bx, cx, tol
    real(sp), intent(out) :: xmin
    interface
       function f(x) result(val)
         import :: sp
         real(sp), intent(in) :: x
         real(sp) :: val
       end function f
    end interface
    real(sp) :: gmin
    real(sp) :: a, b, x1, x2, f1, f2

    a = ax
    b = cx
    x1 = a + C*(b-a)
    x2 = a + R*(b-a)

    f2 = f(x2)

          f1 = f2

          x2 = x1
          f2 = f1
          x1 = a + C*(b-a)
          f1 = f(x1)
       end if
    end do
    xmin = 0.5_sp*(a+b)
    gmin = f(xmin)
  end function golden

  ! Subroutine PROFIL2 – original algorithm with modern syntax
  !=================================================================
  subroutine PROFIL2(MAXA, MHT, LM, NEQ, NEL, NDT, NWK)
    implicit none
    integer, intent(in)               :: NEQ, NEL, NDT
    integer, intent(in)               :: LM(NEL,NDT)
    integer, intent(out)              :: MAXA(NEQ+1)
    integer, intent(out)              :: MHT(NEQ)
    integer, intent(out)              :: NWK

    integer :: KEL, I, LS, KEQ, ME, MK, MM, NEQ1

    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Logging – start of routine
    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    call bot('PROFIL')

    call IZERO(MHT, NEQ)

    do KEL = 1, NEL
       LS = 1000000
       ! Find smallest positive LM entry for this element
       do I = 1, NDT
          if (LM(KEL,I) > 0) then
             if (LM(KEL,I) < LS) LS = LM(KEL,I)
          end if
       end do
       ! Update column heights
       do I = 1, NDT
          if (LM(KEL,I) > 0) then
             ME = LM(KEL,I) - LS
             if (ME > MHT(LM(KEL,I))) MHT(LM(KEL,I)) = ME
          end if
       end do
    end do

    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    ! Compute skyline address vector (MAXA) and total terms (NWK)
    !---------------------------------------------------------------
    NEQ1 = NEQ + 1
    call IZERO(MAXA, NEQ1)

    MAXA(1) = 1
    MAXA(2) = 2
    MK = 0

    if (NEQ > 1) then
       do KEQ = 2, NEQ
          if (MHT(KEQ) > MK) MK = MHT(KEQ)
          MAXA(KEQ+1) = MAXA(KEQ) + MHT(KEQ) + 1
       end do
    end if

    MK = MK + 1
    NWK = MAXA(NEQ1) - MAXA(1)
    MM  = NWK / NEQ

    write(IOUT,1000) NEQ, NWK, MK, MM

    call eot('PROFIL')

    return

program cntab1_demo
  implicit none
  ! Kind parameters – single‑precision real and 4‑byte integer
  integer, parameter :: sp  = selected_real_kind(p=6, r=37)
  integer, parameter :: i4b = selected_int_kind(9)

  integer(i4b), allocatable :: nn(:,:)
  real(sp) :: chisq, df, prob, cramrv, ccc

  ! Hard‑coded contingency table (2 rows × 3 columns)
  allocate(nn(2,3))
  nn = reshape([10_i4b, 20_i4b, 30_i4b, 40_i4b, 50_i4b, 60_i4b], shape(nn))

  call cntab1(nn, chisq, df, prob, cramrv, ccc)

  print *, 'chisq =', chisq
  print *, 'df    =', df
  print *, 'prob  =', prob
  print *, 'cramrv=', cramrv
  print *, 'ccc   =', ccc

contains

  subroutine cntab1(nn, chisq, df, prob, cramrv, ccc)
    implicit none
    integer(i4b), intent(in) :: nn(:,:)
    real(sp),    intent(out) :: chisq, df, prob, cramrv, ccc
    real(sp), parameter :: tiny = 1.0e-30_sp

    integer :: nni, nnj
    real(sp) :: sumn
    real(sp), allocatable :: sumi(:), sumj(:), expctd(:,:)

    ! Row and column marginal totals (converted to real)
    allocate(sumi(size(nn,1)))
    allocate(sumj(size(nn,2)))
    sumi = real( sum(nn, dim=2), sp )
    sumj = real( sum(nn, dim=1), sp )
    sumn = sum(sumi)

    ! Numbers of non‑zero rows / columns
    nni = size(sumi) - count(sumi == 0.0_sp)
    nnj = size(sumj) - count(sumj == 0.0_sp)
    df = real( nni*nnj - nni - nnj + 1, sp )

    ! Expected frequencies under independence
    expctd = outerprod(sumi, sumj) / sumn

    ! Pearson chi‑square statistic
    chisq = sum( (real(nn,sp) - expctd)**2 / (expctd + tiny) )

    ! Significance probability (upper incomplete gamma)
    prob = gammq(0.5_sp*df, 0.5_sp*chisq)

    ! Cramér's V and contingency coefficient
    cramrv = sqrt( chisq / (sumn * min(real(nni-1,sp), real(nnj-1,sp))) )

    na = size(a)
    nb = size(b)
